### H-036 — OIR auto-tick clears an outstanding-investigation chase-up on a wrong or unintended match

| Field                           | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Hazard ID**                   | H-036                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Description**                 | The Outstanding Investigation Requests card's auto-tick (`content-scripts/triage-lens/content.js` `applyOutstandingMatch`/`performOirAutoTick`, gated by `_oirAutoTicked` so it fires once per task) automatically ticks request rows the engine (`engine/outstanding-match.js`) judges CONFIDENT and report-covered/predating, **writing to Medicus server-side with no per-instance confirmation** — unlike the clinician-confirmed bulk tick-off (H-034-adjacent, `confirmBulkTickOff`). The hazard is that an incorrect or unintended match (e.g. an inferred analyte-signature match rather than an explicit panel/group-name link) silently clears a genuinely outstanding chase-up from the patient's worklist, and — because ticking writes to Medicus immediately — this **cannot be reversed from the extension**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **Potential causes**            | The analyte-signature matcher infers a match from name/analyte overlap and a predating date rather than an explicit lab panel/group-name link (unless the "Strict" confidence floor is configured); a coincidental repeat of the same test under a different clinical question; date/clock skew making an unrelated later result appear to predate the request; the write happening before the clinician has looked at the row at all (no confirm step, unlike the bulk path).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Affected users / components** | Clinicians relying on the Outstanding Investigation Requests card to track chase-ups. Components: `content-scripts/triage-lens/content.js` (`applyOutstandingMatch`, `performOirAutoTick`), `engine/outstanding-match.js` (the confidence/predating verdict).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Initial severity**            | 3 (Moderate — a wrongly-cleared chase-up delays follow-up of a genuinely outstanding investigation; the underlying request record and report data are unaffected, only the chase-up's visibility on the worklist)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **Initial likelihood**          | 3 (Possible — runs automatically on every qualifying task view, with no confirmation step)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Initial risk**                | 9                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) **Confidence gate** — only verdicts the engine marks `confident` (not `tentative`) are eligible for `autoTick`; ambiguous matches are flagged inline only, never ticked. (b) **Predating gate** — the matcher rejects a result that postdates the request as "resulted"; only a report/result that genuinely covers the request in time can auto-tick. (c) **Once-per-task guard** (`_oirAutoTicked`) — never re-fires, and never re-ticks a row a clinician has manually unticked. (d) **NEW (Phase 1.4): audit trail** — every auto-tick writes an entry (kind: `'auto'`) to the same `triagelens.oir.auditLog` ring buffer/cap as the clinician-confirmed bulk path (`recordOirAudit`), visible in the options audit viewer. (e) **NEW: undoable-in-spirit review toast** — a non-blocking toast lists exactly what was auto-ticked and offers a **"Review"** action (not "Undo") that scrolls to and flashes the ticked row(s); it is deliberately NOT labelled Undo and does not re-click the checkbox, because ticking writes to Medicus immediately and — per the bulk path's own confirm-dialog text — "cannot be undone from here"; the Review action is itself audited (kind: `'auto-undo'`) so a clinician's follow-up check is also on record. (f) **`oirAutoTick` preference — default OFF as of the 2026-08-22 clinical-safety audit** (it originally shipped default ON "preserving pre-existing behaviour", which contradicted the intended-purpose statement's "no write is automatic" boundary and left this — the product's only machine-initiated write — outside the CSN §6.1 inventory; it is now CSN row **W22** and auto-tick is a deliberate practice opt-in). The inline "resulted (this report)" flag and the clinician-confirmed bulk tick-off remain available either way. (g) The confidence-floor and lookback-window prefs (`oirConfidenceFloor`/`oirLookbackMonths`) let a practice tighten match criteria suite-wide. |
| **Residual severity**           | 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **Residual likelihood**         | 2 (the confidence + predating gate, unchanged by this work, remains the primary preventive control; the audit trail, review toast and pref off-switch added here are detective/governance controls, not preventive ones, so they narrow attributability and give a practice an opt-out rather than lowering the base match-error rate)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Residual risk**               | 6 — Acceptable (ALARP)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Acceptability**               | Accepted (ALARP). The confidence + predating match gate is the primary control. Because a tick cannot be reversed from the extension, the residual risk that remains after any control set is that a wrongly-cleared chase-up must be re-requested via Medicus directly if genuinely needed — the toast states this explicitly, and the CSN known-limitations should record it. Practices with a lower risk tolerance can turn `oirAutoTick` off and rely on the inline flag + clinician-confirmed bulk tick-off only.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

### H-037 — Seen-session queue row dimming de-emphasises a worked-but-unresolved row

| Field                           | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Hazard ID**                   | H-037                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Description**                 | The Investigation Results queue's seen-session dimming (item 4.7, `docs/plans/TRIAGE-LENS-2026-07-02.md`; `content-scripts/triage-lens/content.js` `reapplyQueueSeenDim`/`_seenTasks`) visually dims (opacity ~0.55) queue rows whose task the clinician has already opened this browser session, so unworked rows stand out. The hazard is that a row a clinician opened but did **not** fully action (looked at the result, got interrupted, closed it without completing the necessary follow-up) is now visually de-emphasised, and the clinician may skim past it on a later pass through the queue believing "seen" means "dealt with", when it only means "opened".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Potential causes**            | A clinician opens a task, is interrupted before completing the follow-up, and relies on the dimmed/undimmed contrast rather than the row's actual chip/tint state when re-scanning the queue; automation bias (H-007) — treating the visual de-emphasis itself as a signal of completion rather than of mere prior viewing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Affected users / components** | Clinicians triaging the Investigation Results queue with `queueSeenDimming` enabled. Components: `content-scripts/triage-lens/content.js` (`_seenTasks`, `reapplyQueueSeenDim`, `clearQueueSeenDim`, the `runDetailVerdict` seen-marking hook), `content-scripts/triage-lens/hud.css` (`.ch-row-seen`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **Initial severity**            | 3 (Moderate — a de-emphasised row could delay a clinician's attention returning to a genuinely unresolved task; no data is hidden, changed, or suppressed, and every chip/tint/status-bar count is completely unaffected)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Initial likelihood**          | 2 (Unlikely — opt-in and default OFF; requires both enabling the pref AND a clinician misreading dim-vs-undimmed as a completion signal rather than a "previously opened" signal)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Initial risk**                | 6                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) **Visual only, suppresses nothing from the engine** — chip content, severity tint, and the triage status-bar counts (item 1.2) are computed completely independently of `_seenTasks`/dimming; a dimmed row's underlying data is identical to an undimmed one. (b) **Hard safety gate: a row is NEVER dimmed while tinted red or amber** — `reapplyQueueSeenDim` only adds `ch-row-seen` to a row that does NOT currently carry `ch-row-sev-red`/`ch-row-sev-amber`, checked fresh against the row's live tint class on every `refreshQueueChips` cycle, never a one-off snapshot taken when the task was opened. An escalation is never dimmed away. (c) **Auto-undim on severity change** — because the tint-class gate in (b) is re-evaluated every cycle against `_queueResultCache`'s current value (not a cached flag), a previously-dimmed row that later re-grades red/amber (a new result lands) automatically loses `ch-row-seen` on the very next `refreshQueueChips` pass, with no separate "undo" code path to get wrong — verified in `test-queue-injection-smoke.js` Layer 23. (d) **Session-local, never persisted** — `_seenTasks` is a plain in-memory `Set`, never written to `chrome.storage`, and is forgotten on page reload; it cannot silently accumulate or leak between sessions or devices. (e) **Opt-in, default OFF** (`queueSeenDimming` pref) — the most snooze-adjacent feature in the plan, so the conservative default is off; a practice must deliberately enable it. (f) **Never hides** — dimming uses `opacity`, never `display:none`/removal; a dimmed row remains fully visible, scrollable, clickable, and counted identically in the status bar. (g) Severity row tint (item 1.3) and the triage status bar (item 1.2) remain the primary, always-on signals of what still needs attention; dimming is a secondary scan aid layered on top, not a replacement for either. |
| **Residual severity**           | 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Residual likelihood**         | 1 (the never-dim-an-alert-row gate and the auto-undim it gives for free are preventive controls that directly close the failure mode this hazard describes — a row cannot stay dimmed once it needs attention — leaving only the narrower risk of a clinician relying on the dim state itself as a completion signal, which the opt-in default-off posture and the "seen ≠ actioned" framing mitigate)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Residual risk**               | 3 — Acceptable (ALARP)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Acceptability**               | Accepted (ALARP). The never-dim-an-alert-row gate combined with the auto-undim behaviour is the primary control: by construction, a row can only ever be dimmed while its own cached severity is clear/none or unassessed, and it stops being dimmed the instant that changes. This suppresses nothing — it is a purely additive scan aid, distinct from the excluded "alert snooze / temporal suppression" capability (standing decision, `docs/plans/TRIAGE-LENS-2026-07-02.md` header) which this feature is deliberately NOT: dimming never lowers a row's severity, never removes a chip, and never affects the status-bar counts.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

| **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) **No affirmative verdict state, by construction** — the UI never renders an affirmative safe/clear state, tick, or green all-clear; the words "safe" and "clear" appear only inside explicit NEGATIONS of the automation-bias misread ("No flag ≠ safe to sign", "≠ all clear"), which is deliberately more protective than avoiding the words. The no-flag state renders as "no monitoring flags recorded" with a permanent inline "≠ all clear" caveat (`signing.js` `verdictHtml`). (b) **Fixed honest-state header** — "Monitoring shown is what is recorded, not what is true. No flag ≠ safe to sign — verify in the record before authorising." is a structural part of the surface (`.sg-honest`), not a dismissable notice. (c) **Fail-visible record reads** — an incomplete or failed record read renders as an amber "record not read — check manually" error row and sorts ABOVE no-flag rows (`sortSigningRows` bands: unknown outranks a recorded all-clear); it can never be conflated with a clear row. (d) **Read-only** — the module has no write path of any kind; authorisation happens exclusively in Medicus with Medicus's own signing screen and its own safeguards in front of the prescriber. (e) **Same engine, same rules** — verdicts come from the identical `evaluatePatient` pipeline Sentinel/Sweep already display, with practice org/custom rule overlays applied; this surface adds no new clinical logic to be wrong. (f) **Requested-drug flag is additive salience only** — the "requested" tag raises attention on the riskiest rows; it never suppresses or reorders anything downward. (g) Intended-purpose statement and tab help both frame the surface as context display; the frozen statement's exclusion of prescribing decisions is cited in the module header comment as an editing constraint on future copy. (h) **Wrong-patient guard (H-001 adjacency)** — every task is resolved to its own patient UUID via the task-overview endpoint before any verdict is attached; verdicts are shared between rows ONLY on an identical resolved UUID. No name/DOB-based grouping exists anywhere in the module (reviewed out pre-merge, 2026-07-07): demographic strings are never treated as identity, and a task whose patient cannot be resolved renders as an error row. (i) **Renal fact is verbatim + always dated (v3.156.0)** — the row's eGFR display is the latest RECORDED value copied verbatim with its age permanently attached (value is never rendered without date/age); no threshold, band, or dose logic is computed from it, and its absence is only remarked on rows already carrying a monitoring flag. Mitigates out-of-context display (H-010) for this fact. (j) **Location-filter hidden-red-flag callout (v3.158.0)** — the location filter pills are session-only (never persisted, so a forgotten filter cannot silently hide rows across a return visit) and a narrowed view is never silent — the count of rows hidden by the active filter is shown, and any hidden rows carrying a RED monitoring flag are specifically called out by count in red, distinct from the general hidden-count. The monitoring pass evaluates every row regardless of the active filter; filtering only affects what is displayed, never what is checked. (k) **Collection-location flag is verbatim, routing-only (v3.157.0)** — the collection-location chip is copied verbatim from the task row's own `collectionLocationName` (zero extra fetches, no derived logic) and is explicitly never rendered in red/amber — it is dispensing-routing information, not a monitoring or safety signal, and its absence (Medicus records none) is simply omitted rather than flagged. (l) **Wrong-patient guard reliability fix (v3.156.1)** — the constructed `/tasks/data/{list-slug}/overview/{id}` path used by control (h)'s per-task UUID resolution failed universally on first live use (the live overview endpoint's slug differs from the task-list slug); the row's own validated `overviewURL` — the same pointer Medicus itself links, validated with the identical pattern the queue bridge uses — is now the authoritative resolution path, with the constructed path retained only as a fallback. Before this fix the failure mode was every row rendering as a fail-visible "record not read" error (control (c)) — never a wrong-patient chip — confirming the fail-visible design held even while the resolution pipeline was completely non-functional. (m) **Empty-state warmth does not create an affirmative verdict (v3.159.0)** — when every task type is ticked and no location filter is active, a genuinely-empty pile shows one fixed line ("Pile's clear — nothing waiting on you") acknowledging finished _work_, never monitoring status; a narrowed or type-filtered empty view keeps the neutral wording instead, so the warm state can never be produced by hiding rows rather than clearing them. This is consistent with, not an exception to, control (a)'s no-affirmative-verdict design. (n) **Combination re-display only (v3.161.0)** — the drug-combination chips shown at signing are the engine's EXISTING evaluations of the practice's configured combination rules (CSO-reviewed alert library + practice-authored), computed in the same `evaluatePatient` pass; the surface adds NO new clinical rule content, and the "in request" tag (a requested drug forming one leg of a flagged combination, e.g. an acute NSAID completing the ACEi+diuretic AKI cluster) is additive salience under the same doctrine as control (f). Red combinations join the riskiest-first banding and the hidden-red filter note, so surfacing them can only raise attention, never lower it. (o) **Awareness tier deliberately not surfaced at signing (v3.161.0)** — only alert (red) and caution (amber) combination tiers render here; the 'noted' awareness tier stays in Monitoring, so salience at the point of authorisation is reserved for act-on-it-now combinations and alarm dilution cannot erode the red tier (`COMBO_STATUS_LEVEL`, regression-tested). |

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Acceptability**               | Accepted (ALARP). The surface reorganises attention over work the prescriber already has, using rules the practice already runs; the failure mode it could add (skipping the record because the panel looked quiet) is addressed by never rendering an affirmative state and by ranking unknowns above quiet rows. Net effect is expected to be protective: overdue-monitoring repeats that today get signed blind become visible before authorisation.
