### H-045 — Breach-risk strip under-reports or over-trusts Medicus's own urgency flag

| Field                           | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Hazard ID**                   | H-045                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Description**                 | The `#slaBreachStrip` (v3.177.0) surfaces a count and oldest-age of open requests whose Medicus `priority`/`priorityDisplay` reads urgent. The flag is an unvalidated upstream intake/triage label; a clinically urgent request the intake mislabelled routine is invisible to the strip, and a hidden strip (zero urgent) could be misread as "no urgent work exists".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Potential causes**            | Upstream mislabelling; priority field schema change; Request Monitor disabled/misconfigured; stale cached bucket state.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Affected users / components** | Duty GP / care navigator relying on the strip: `shared/sla-breach-core.js`, `shared/request-monitor.js`, `side-panel/panel.js`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **Initial severity**            | 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Initial likelihood**          | 2                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Initial risk**                | 6                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) Strictly additive — displays a warning band only; never suppresses, reorders, hides or actions any request. (b) No green/"all clear" state: hidden when nothing at breach risk, so it cannot render a reassuring verdict. (c) Fail-visible: items with no readable priority field render an explicit "urgency unknown — check queue" state, never a silent zero. (d) Reuses the Request Monitor's existing poll cadence and cached state; strip inert when the monitor is disabled (no half-live display). (e) `test-sla-breach-core.js` pins urgent detection, unknown-priority path and amber/red boundaries. |
| **Residual severity**           | 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Residual likelihood**         | 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Residual risk**               | 3 — Acceptable (ALARP)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Acceptability**               | Accepted (ALARP) — CSO reviewed and signed off 2026-07-22 (Dr Dave Triska), recorded via Dave's session instruction delegating completion to his digital twin. Additive-only, no all-clear state, fail-visible `unknown` path verified in `shared/sla-breach-core.js` and pinned by `test-sla-breach-core.js`. **Condition (applied same commit):** CSN limitation 43 states that when Request Monitor is disabled the strip is _silent_ (inert), so an absent strip is never read as "urgent breaches are being watched". The strip is a prompt to check the queue, not a substitute for triage of every request.  |

### H-046 — Pending-result cross-link chip serves a stale or wrong-patient severity

| Field                           | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Hazard ID**                   | H-046                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Description**                 | The `.ch-q-pending` chip (v3.177.0) tells a request-queue row's clinician that this session graded a red/amber result for the same patient. A stale index entry (result since actioned/superseded) or a mis-resolved task→patient link could surface a wrong or outdated "pending urgent result" claim — a deprioritisation/wrong-patient harm in both directions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Potential causes**            | Patient-keyed index outliving its taskUuid-keyed source cache entry; task→patient mis-resolution; client-side grid re-sort landing chips on the wrong row.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Affected users / components** | Request-queue triagers: `shared/pending-result-index.js`, `content-scripts/triage-lens/content.js` (B-substrate, `_queueResultCache`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Initial severity**            | 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Initial likelihood**          | 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Initial risk**                | 9                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) Index entries are pointers that die with their source severity — hooked at all four teardown paths (TTL prune, priorityDisplay invalidation, config invalidation, re-grade to null/none/error); queries read only live entries. (b) Patient match by resolved UUID only, never name/DOB; re-resolution vacates the old patient bucket. (c) Chip placement rides the durable row map, so the H-6-class sort canary suppresses chips on any client re-sort (absence, never wrong row). (d) Every chip carries its data age in text and title ("graded 12m ago") and is same-session only. (e) Escalate-only: no "no pending result" state exists. (f) `test-pending-result-index.js` pins the dies-with-source lifecycle. |
| **Residual severity**           | 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Residual likelihood**         | 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Residual risk**               | 3 — Acceptable (ALARP)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Acceptability**               | Accepted (ALARP) — CSO reviewed and signed off 2026-07-22 (Dr Dave Triska), recorded via Dave's session instruction delegating completion to his digital twin. Dies-with-source lifecycle confirmed at all four teardown hooks in `content.js` (TTL prune, priorityDisplay invalidation, config invalidation, re-grade-to-null/error), UUID-only patient match, sort-canary-safe durable-map placement, same-session and age-stamped in text; escalate-only with no "no pending result" state. Pinned by `test-pending-result-index.js` including the outlives-source invariant.                                                                                                                                            |

### H-047 — Repeat-contact chip miscounts, or its local ledger leaks/fabricates contact history

| Field                           | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Hazard ID**                   | H-047                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Description**                 | The `.ch-q-repeat` chip (v3.177.0) claims "Nth contact in 14d" (rolling local ledger) or "N open requests · this patient" (session tier). A miscount over-escalates (fatigue) or under-counts (missed deterioration signal); the ledger itself is a device-local trail of patientUuid+date pairs that must not fabricate history on another machine or carry identifiable content.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Potential causes**            | Task→patient mis-resolution; ledger restore onto a machine that never observed the contacts; taskUuid reuse; unbounded growth.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Affected users / components** | Request-queue triagers: `shared/contact-ledger.js`, `content-scripts/triage-lens/content.js`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Initial severity**            | 2                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Initial likelihood**          | 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Initial risk**                | 6                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) Ledger stores UUIDs + ISO dates only — no names, no free text, no clinical content; UUID-shape validated on write. (b) Deliberately excluded from suite backups (event-ledger doctrine): restoring an observational trail elsewhere would fabricate a false contact history. (c) Bounded: 28-day retention, 14-day query window, 500-patient / 20-contact / 2000-task caps with oldest-first pruning; coalesced dirty-checked writes. (d) Wording factual-observational ("3rd contact in 14d"), never diagnostic; amber-only; no "1st contact" state. (e) Durable-map placement (sort-canary-safe); session tier counts only distinct taskUuids actually resolved this session. |
| **Residual severity**           | 2                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Residual likelihood**         | 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Residual risk**               | 2 — Acceptable                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Acceptability**               | Accepted — CSO reviewed and signed off 2026-07-22 (Dr Dave Triska), recorded via Dave's session instruction delegating completion to his digital twin. Ledger holds pseudonymous UUIDs + ISO dates only (no names, no content), UUID-shape-validated, bounded and oldest-first pruned, and CI-guaranteed out of suite backups (`test-backup-coverage.js` allowlist). The machine-local-disclosure doctrine already applied to H-040/H-042 applies here: the patientUuid is pseudonymous PII resolvable only within an authenticated Medicus session, and the trail never leaves the workstation. Factual-observational wording, amber-only, no first-contact state.                 |

(c) A re-opened same-UUID task reading as "carried" from original first-seen is the intended escalation, stated factually ("carried over 4d"), never diagnostically. |

Complementary-by-construction: fires only on the first-seen-predates-displayed-date bounce signature and defers to the taskAge-red signal, so it cannot double-signal or overstate against the row's own stronger age indicator. | **Description**                 | The GP → reception quick-actions composer (v3.197.0, `content-scripts/reception-quick-actions.js`) pre-fills a task's **Internal comment** box with one composed sentence ("Book F2F appt with any GP, within 2 weeks."). It writes TEXT ONLY — it books nothing, assigns nothing and submits nothing. Four misreadings are possible. (i) **Inserted ≠ submitted:** the GP taps chips, presses Insert, then navigates away without pressing Medicus's own Submit — the instruction evaporates while the GP believes reception was told. (ii) **Automation bias:** picking chips from a structured menu feels like _doing_ the thing ("I ticked it, so it's booked") in a way typing free text does not — the chips look like a booking form and are not one. (iii) **Wrong-task insert:** a mid-flight SPA navigation between picking the chips and pressing Insert could append task A's instruction into task B's comment box. (iv) **Timeframe read as a safety net:** "Within 2 weeks" looks like a deadline the system will chase; nothing in the suite tracks, chases or escalates it — it is a sentence a human must act on. A fifth, slower failure is **config drift**: the who-list is unvalidated free text, so a leaver's name still composes a perfectly readable instruction nobody can act on.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Potential causes**            | Insert pressed but Submit not pressed (interruption, phone call, "the box has text in it so it's done"); a structured chip UI implying execution rather than composition (H-007 automation bias); SPA re-render/navigation between chip selection and insert (the H-043 race, same surface family); a deadline phrase read as a system-enforced recall (H-040's safety-net-of-record misreading); practice `triagelens.quickActions` who/action lists going stale as staff join and leave, or edited into ambiguous wording.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Affected users / components** | GPs composing reception instructions on task overviews, and the reception/PST staff who read the resulting comment: `content-scripts/reception-quick-actions.js` (widget, insert, Submit highlight), `shared/quick-actions-core.js` (`composeLine`/`appendToComment`, pinned by `test-quick-actions-core.js`), the practice list editor in `options/options.js` (Quick Actions section), `shared/io/triage-io.js` (list backup). Cross-references H-007 (automation bias), H-040 (ledger over-trusted as safety-netting system of record), H-043 (wrong-target write after a mid-flight SPA navigation). | **Initial severity**            | 3 (a lost or mis-targeted reception instruction delays an appointment, a blood test or a call-back; it does not itself alter the clinical record) | **Initial likelihood**          | 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Initial risk**                | 9                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) **Text-only by construction** — the widget's entire effect is an append into a field the clinician still reads and submits; it makes no API call, clicks no control, and books/sends/submits nothing. `composeLine()` and `appendToComment()` return strings. (b) **Explicit, gated Insert** — nothing is ever inserted automatically; the Insert button is disabled until an Action chip is picked, and the exact sentence is shown in a live preview before it is pressed. (c) **Append-only** — `appendToComment()` never clears, truncates or rewrites what the clinician already typed (the existing text is always an untouched prefix; pinned in `test-quick-actions-core.js`). (d) **Submit is highlighted, never clicked** — after an insert the card's own Submit/"Submit as new" control is ringed (scrolled to only when off-screen, so the freshly-inserted text is not yanked away — the routine-rx `highlight()` treatment), making the outstanding human step visually obvious; pressing it remains the clinician's act. A capture-phase listener observes (never prevents, never synthesises) a click on that control solely to clear the pending reminder below — and deliberately claims nothing on it, because a click is not a successful submit. (e) **Wording states the limit at every step, and the un-submitted state does not time out** (v3.204.0) — the collapsed strip reads "Reception instruction — _writes text only — books nothing_", the two-step flow is numbered in place ("1. Insert into comment ↓" / "2. Then press “Submit as new” below.", the submit label read live off the card's own control), the inserted sentence is echoed back verbatim ("Added to the comment below: …"), a transient flash confirms the write ("Text added to the internal comment below. Read it, then press “Submit as new”."), and a **timerless** amber reminder — "**Not yet submitted** — press “Submit as new” below. Until you do, reception sees nothing." — plus a "not yet submitted" pill in the always-visible header strip persist until the clinician clicks Submit, navigates away, or empties the box (an interruption cannot outlive the warning). The words "Done", "Sent" and "Booked" are deliberately never used, and `test-reception-quick-actions-ui.js` pins the safety strings, the no-completion-claim rule, the no-click rule, the append-only write and the timerless reminder in CI. (f) **Task identity pinned and re-verified** — the task UUID is pinned when the composer opens or the first chip is picked and re-checked synchronously at insert; a mismatch resets the selections and shows "Task changed — reopen and re-pick." instead of writing (H-043 discipline, the create-task section of `content-scripts/task-actions-panel.js`, formerly `task-inline.js`), and an SPA path change clears all state and removes the widget. The textarea is re-located fresh in the live DOM at every insert, never cached. (g) **No safety-net claim** — the composer displays no due-date, no tracking state and no follow-up list; the timeframe is rendered as ordinary prose inside the clinician's own sentence, and the options page states in terms that timeframes are deadlines for a human to meet, that "Usual GP" can bounce back, and that names are unvalidated free text to be kept current when staff change. (h) **No patient data persisted** — the free-text note is transient JS state and never reaches `chrome.storage`; only the practice's chip lists are stored (`triagelens.quickActions`, backed up via the triage scope). (i) **All rendered config strings escaped** — `esc()` in the widget, `escHtml`/`escAttr` on the options page; the core carries markup as inert text and never renders HTML. (j) **Composer pinned in CI** — `test-quick-actions-core.js` pins every canonical sentence verbatim, the append-only invariant and the config sanitiser (clamps, caps, prototype-key rejection), so a phrasing or safety drift fails the build rather than reaching a receptionist. |

The feature adds no automation and no new claim: it composes a sentence the GP was already typing by hand into a box the GP already had to submit, and it makes the remaining human step (Submit) more visible than before, not less. Residual risk sits in wording and habit rather than in mechanism — the CSO review should focus on the shipped chip labels (do they read as instructions a receptionist can act on without interpretation?), on the "not yet submitted" wording, and on whether practices need a prompt to review the who-list when staff leave. **Field evidence + remediation, 2026-07-31 (v3.204.0):** practice feedback with screenshots showed that on flex-row field containers the injected widget crushed the Internal-comment textarea to a few px, rendering the inserted sentence one character per line — controls (b)/(e) were materially degraded in live use ("the clinician still reads the comment" is not true if they physically cannot read it), and the practice also reported the Insert button being missed and the insert not being recognised as having worked (the H-007/H-049(i)-(ii) misreadings observed in the field). Remediated in v3.204.0: parent flex-wrap + full-row widget with a measure-and-rehoist self-heal (fixture now carries the flex-row layout), inserted-sentence echo, numbered two-step flow, and the timerless pending reminder described in controls (d)/(e). **The v3.204.0 layout fix did not hold in the field** (same-day screenshot: textarea still crushed — the crushing flex container is not always the direct parent, and the one-shot inject-time measure is stale once Vue re-applies its layout); v3.204.1 replaced it with a hard CSS `min-width: 220px !important` on the following-sibling textarea (min-width beats flex-shrink whichever ancestor crushes, and survives inline-style rewrites), an escalating `fixCrushedLayout()` (5-level ancestor un-nowrap → textarea full-row patch → widget hoist, each step measured), and a continuous re-check on every observed DOM churn rather than at inject time only — all host-node style patches recorded and restored on widget removal, and all three layers pinned in `test-reception-quick-actions-ui.js`. A third same-day report showed the container is a **grid**, which flex-targeted fixes cannot see (a sibling shifts every auto-placed item one cell; min-width overflows a fixed track); v3.204.2 stops competing in the container's layout altogether — insertion climbs out of single-child wrapper shells, the widget spans all grid columns (`grid-column: 1 / -1`), a grid-collapse escalation and an inline textarea min-width back it up, and an exhausted guard now dumps the ancestor chain under the `ch-debug` flag so any further failure is evidence-driven. Mechanism unchanged — text-only append, gated Insert, Submit highlighted never clicked, task UUID re-verified.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

It suggests only: it books nothing, sends nothing and assigns nothing, and the receptionist confirms or overrides it. Three misreadings are possible. (i) **Suggestion read as a decision** — non-clinical staff treat the card as the practice's clinical instruction and route the patient to a pharmacy, nurse or paramedic without offering, or arranging, a clinician; the presentation was outside the short red-flag list (the H-024 failure mode) and needed a GP. (ii) **Wrong age, wrong route** — the route is age-sensitive (Pharmacy First bands, the under-1 and under-5 floors); an age taken from the wrong open record, or guessed, produces a confidently-worded suggestion for the wrong patient. (iii) **Editable routing** — `disposition` blocks live in `rules/reception-pathways.json` and in practice-authored/edited pathways, so a practice edit, an LLM-authored pack or a crafted backup could in principle propose a non-clinician destination for a presentation that must always see a clinician. LLM-authored pathway declaring a routing block that was never clinically reviewed; a fork of a clinician-only pathway relabelled with a permissive domain; a restored backup carrying a routing sign-off from another practice; shipped disposition blocks enabled before CSO sign-off. | **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) **Suggestion-only by construction** — the engine returns a plain object; nothing books, sends, assigns or submits anything. The receptionist confirms or overrides, and the decision is theirs. (b) **The fallback line is part of the artefact** — "Or a clinician callback if the patient prefers — always offer it." is a code constant rendered with every suggestion on screen _and_ written into the pasted capture text, so the reading clinician sees that the offer was made. (c) **Red-flag gate** — any positive red flag, and any unanswered one, suppresses the card entirely (`status: 'withheld'`); a suggestion cannot coexist with an open safety question. (d) **Frozen clinician-only sets** — `CLINICIAN_ONLY_IDS` (`mental-health`, `gu-male`, `gyn-female`, `general`) and `CLINICIAN_ONLY_DOMAINS` (`mental_health`, `gu_male`, `gyn_female`) are constants in engine code, keyed on the **bundled** id and applied **after** override resolution: a fork that relabels its domain still produces clinician-only output. `resolveEffectivePathways` additionally **rejects** an override that would downgrade a clinician-only bundled pathway and flags it as `overrideInvalid`, so the practice sees the rejection. Sensitive pathways (mental-health) render nothing at all. (e) **Safeguarding bypasses routing** — a positive `safeguarding: true` red flag is a positive red flag, so no suggestion renders, and the banner and capture text carry the duty-clinician-plus-safeguarding-lead escalation. (f) **Hard age floor** — confirmed age under 1 is clinician-only; under 5 never reaches `anp` or `paramedic` (no paediatric-competence flag exists, so the floor is unconditional); the floor is applied to the **override** control too, so the UI cannot offer what the engine refuses. (g) **Confirmed age only** — the age is one the receptionist explicitly entered on the call, never inherited from the open-record snapshot, never autosaved into a draft; an unknown or out-of-range age fails **closed** to a GP appointment. Pharmacy First suggestions re-check the pathway's own Pharmacy First age band through the same gate as the hint line. (h) **Custom and edited packs are clinician-only by default** — they suggest nothing but a clinician until a `reception.routingAttestation` recording a **CSO or partner** name, role and timestamp exists (options UI: "routing sign-off: CSO or partner only"); it is revocable in one click, strictly re-validated on backup import (invalid → dropped, never partially stored), and surfaced as a warning at import preview. (i) **Audit trail in the pasted text** — the suggested route, its basis, and whether the receptionist confirmed or overrode it (with a free-text reason) are written into the capture block; **withheld** dispositions are recorded too (`Disposition withheld: red flag positive` / `clinician-only pathway`), so a significant-event review can reconstruct what the tool did and did not say. This is where the NHSE record-the-navigation requirement lands. (j) **Closed, fail-invalid schema** — `domain`, `allowed`, `default` and the three-key `when` vocabulary are closed enums; an unknown destination, condition or extra field makes the whole pathway invalid rather than partially honoured, and sanitisation whitelist-copies the block on every editor save and backup import. (k) **Governance** — all shipped disposition blocks are DRAFT pending CSO sign-off (recorded in `specVersion`); pathways still ship disabled behind the H-024 disclaimer; every capture still carries the "not a clinical assessment — clinician to review" footer. (l) **Guardrail truth-table tests** — `test-reception-disposition.js` pins the precedence order, the adversarial `mental-health` fork, both age floors, the unconfirmed-age fail-closed path, Pharmacy First fail-closed eligibility, the attestation gate and shape validation, and the presence of the fallback line on every suggestion. |

Triska (CSO) — review performed by delegated virtual-Dave agent at Dave's instruction, 2026-07-28 (chat); recorded in `docs/cso-review-ledger.json`. E decides who the patient sees, so its hazard outranks the booking work in plan section D, and the review went through the shipped blocks one at a time rather than accepting them as a set. **Findings.** (i) The four Pharmacy First pathways whose age band maps 1:1 onto a single named PF condition (sore throat 5+, otitis media 1–17, sinusitis 12+, UTI in women 16–64) are **accepted as shipped** — the age gate is a fair proxy for eligibility there, the engine re-checks it, and it fails closed on unknown age. (ii) The `rash` block's automatic Pharmacy First rule was **REMOVED at review** and the change is part of this sign-off: that one age band stands in for three PF conditions with different bands, and the pathway's own match terms legitimately catch cellulitis, which Pharmacy First does not cover — an age-only gate would have confidently suggested a pharmacy for a rash the pharmacist cannot treat, delaying oral antibiotics by a day. `pharmacy_first` remains selectable by the receptionist there; the tool no longer asserts an eligibility it cannot test. (iii) `cough`, `backpain` and `feverish-child` ship with **empty rule lists** — they suggest nothing but a GP appointment and merely permit ANP/paramedic as a human override — which is more conservative than plan E proposed and is accepted as the right posture for a first release. (iv) The suggestion and fallback wording were read as a receptionist would say them aloud and are accepted unchanged; the mandatory fallback line doing double duty on screen and in the pasted text is the control that makes the card a suggestion in practice and not just in documentation. (v) The custom-routing CSO/partner sign-off **should** remain available: without it a practice that authors its own pack gets clinician-only routing forever and will route around the tool instead. Any report of a patient-safety incident where a disposition suggestion contributed is treated as a significant safety event and triggers immediate CSO review and suspension of the routing blocks pending review.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

| **Description**                 | The Reception module gains a third card that **books a real appointment** into Medicus (`createAppointment`) from the side panel: appointment type, a specific day or a 1–4 week window search, a slot, a reason, and the patient-facing confirmation channels. This is the suite's **first clinical write surface aimed at non-clinical staff**, and it is exposed to two distinct failure classes. (i) **Wrong patient.** Two identity sources exist in the suite and can legitimately disagree — the reception snapshot resolves the **active** tab, while the booking shim's `detectMedicusTab` resolves the **first matching** Medicus tab, active or not (plan D1.2). A front desk routinely has several Medicus tabs open, and the receptionist may switch tab, take another call, or have the record change under them between opening the card and pressing Confirm; a booking committed against a stale or divergent identity puts an appointment on a stranger's record, and the intended patient is left with none. Same class as H-043, with a busier and less clinically-trained operator. (ii) **Unsafe capture.** A Book button rendered while a red flag is positive or still unanswered invites the desk to convert an escalation into an appointment slot — the automation-bias failure H-024 and H-050 describe, one step worse because a booking is an action rather than a suggestion. A mental-health/sensitive call is the sharpest version: what to offer someone in distress is a clinician's decision, not a slot picked off a list mid-call. Secondary exposures: the create payload's `bookingConfirmationRecipients` fires patient SMS/email, which both older booking surfaces send silently; a slot reservation abandoned on any exit path locks that slot for every other booker in the practice; and an unbounded window search is a self-inflicted load problem on the practice scheduler.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

and confirming; a patient identity captured once and reused later, the exact gap H-043 was raised for; the floating pop-out window sitting over a different Medicus tab from the one it is reading; capture deliberately working with no record open, so an "ambient" record is available to book against; automation bias applied to a structured booking control by staff for whom the suite is the authority in the room (H-007); a pre-selected appointment type or auto-picked earliest slot being accepted without being chosen; interruption between reserving a slot and completing (or abandoning) the booking; confirmation channels defaulted invisibly so a patient receives an SMS nobody chose to send. | **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) **Open-record hard gate** — with no patient context (or a patient the panel cannot resolve to a record uuid) the card renders visibly **disabled** with "Open the caller's record in Medicus first — booking stays off until the panel can see who you're booking." Capture still works with no record open; booking never does, and never against an ambient one. (b) **One documented identity source** — booking identity is the Sentinel snapshot of the **ACTIVE** Medicus tab (`chrome.tabs.query({active:true, currentWindow:true})`), i.e. the same record whose name the patient card is showing; the source is named in a comment at the function that reads it. (c) **Two-source agreement before the panel arms** — the host's active-tab patient and a fresh `detectMedicusTab`/`detectPatientId` resolution must be equal before any appointment type is even loaded; if they differ the panel refuses to arm and says so, rather than offering a Book button it cannot trust. (d) **Pinned, then re-verified at commit (both id AND site)** — the patient uuid and `apiBase` are pinned when the panel arms, and immediately before `createAppointment` the tab is re-detected and `verifyBookingIdentity()` requires pinned == freshly-detected == currently-displayed on **both**. Any mismatch, and any value that cannot be resolved, aborts: the reservation is released, a plain "nothing was booked" message is shown and no create is issued. This is the booking section of `content-scripts/task-actions-panel.js` (formerly `booking-inline.js`) H-043 discipline (re-verify at commit), not slots.js's older capture-once. The state instance is pinned across every await (`const s = st`), so a late resolution cannot land in another booking's state. (e) **Name + DOB read-back with an explicit tick** — the confirm step shows the patient's name, DOB and NHS number prominently with "This is the right patient"; the Confirm button is disabled until it is ticked, and the tick is re-required for every slot. Fineprint is not a control; a deliberate act is. (f) **Red-flag suppression** — no booking is possible whenever any red flag is positive **or** unanswered, using the SAME `evaluateRedFlags` call that drives the disposition card (`redFlagState()`, written once, used twice). The two states are presented differently, per the CSO decision of 2026-07-28 (review question 4 below): a **positive** flag **hides the card entirely** — a greyed Book button under a duty-escalation banner still reads as "a booking is expected here", and there is nothing to unlock; an **unanswered** flag leaves a one-line note in its place ("Answer every red-flag question first — the booking option appears once they are all answered"), because unanswered is the normal state at the start of every capture and a card that is simply absent teaches the desk to book the same appointment in Medicus or the Slots tab instead, outside every control in this list. If a flag is flipped to YES while a slot is held, the gate closes on the same change hook and the reservation is released. (g) **Sensitive pathways never book** — mental-health and any pathway marked `sensitive` suppress the card unconditionally, red flags or not, matching H-050's no-disposition-output posture. (h) **No pre-selection, no auto-pick** — the appointment type select opens on "Choose appointment type…" (unlike slots.js, which pre-picks a lone type) and no slot is ever pre-selected; both are the receptionist's explicit choice, and the chosen type/slot/reason are written into the capture text (`Booked: <type> — <date/time> — reason: <reason>`) so the reviewing clinician sees what reception booked. (i) **Confirmation channels visible and editable** — `bookingConfirmationRecipientOptions` render as checkboxes at the confirm step and the payload carries **exactly** the ticked subset; un-ticking everything sends nothing. Default remains all-checked (current suite behaviour, now visible) pending the D2 capture of Medicus's own default, which is recorded as a `TODO(D2 spike)` in code. (j) **Reservation released on every exit** — gate closure, Back, the panel unmounting, `destroy()`, pathway-tile navigation, the picker re-rendering on an Options storage change, the summary view, and module `cleanup()`; plus a `pagehide` listener for panel/window close, which reaches the server because `releaseReservation` in the core sends `keepalive: true` (plan D1.3). Five call sites are asserted in CI. (k) **Panel-only ruling** — the pop-out shell (detected by path) renders a one-line "Booking lives in the docked side panel" note instead of the panel. A slot list and a write flow in a narrow always-on-top window that can sit over a _different_ Medicus tab is precisely the identity hazard (c)/(d) exist to kill; recorded deliberately, the same convention as the panel-only demand strips. (l) **No persistence** — no booking, slot, reservation or patient state ever reaches `chrome.storage`; draft autosave remains capture-fields-only. All booking state dies with the card. (m) **No third copy of the booking flow** — every endpoint call goes through `shared/booking-core.js` via the slots shim; the panel contains no endpoint path, no `fetch`, and no credentialed request options (asserted in CI). The window-search caps (≤28 days, ≤4 concurrent, abort on the first 429/5xx, stop at 30 slots) live in the core, not in this UI, so a future copy of the UI cannot raise them. (n) **Truth-table tests** — `test-reception-booking.js` drives the gate over **all 32** combinations of its five inputs against an independently-stated precedence order, the identity comparator over its full mismatch/unresolvable matrix, the window-mode mapping (including fail-closed on an unknown mode), the recipient-subset mapping, and the capture-line formatting; plus source guards that the re-verify happens **before** the create call, that the abort releases the reservation, and that reception tears the panel down on every exit path. |

| **Acceptability**               | **Accepted (ALARP) — CSO REVIEWED AND SIGNED OFF 2026-07-28**, with one control changed at review and three deploying-organisation conditions. Signed off: Dr D. Triska (CSO) — review performed by delegated virtual-Dave agent at Dave's instruction, 2026-07-28 (chat); recorded in `docs/cso-review-ledger.json`. The Phase 0 prerequisite is met: the frozen statement is re-issued and signed as v3.202.0 (`docs/INTENDED-PURPOSE.md`), naming non-clinical staff and this booking capability; CSN §6.1 gains the missing W12 row for this surface. **The four review questions, answered.** **(1) Should reception hold a booking capability in this practice at all? — Yes.** Reception books appointments in Medicus all day; the honest comparison is not "booking versus no booking" but "booking through this panel versus the same receptionist doing it unassisted in Medicus", and on every identity axis the panel is the stricter of the two (Medicus will happily let them book whatever record they have open, with no two-source agreement, no commit-time re-verify and no DOB tick). The one axis where it is worse is that it sits underneath a clinical capture form, which is what controls (f) and (g) exist for. **(2) Is name + DOB read-back sufficient, or should NHS number be spoken back too? — Name and DOB stand; do not add an NHS-number read-back.** Name plus DOB is the identity check reception already uses on the telephone and can perform against a caller who has nothing to hand. Requiring an NHS number invites the receptionist to read it _out_ to an unverified caller, which is a disclosure risk introduced to solve an identity problem already solved. The NHS number remains **displayed** at the confirm step for the receptionist's own cross-check against the record, which is where it belongs. **(3) Should the default all-channels confirmation stand? — For now, yes; it is not the end state.** This release strictly improves on both older surfaces (which send every channel silently); making the channels visible and editable is the substantive change. When the D2 capture records what Medicus's own UI pre-selects, **match Medicus** — the patient's expectation of what a booking sends is set by the host system, not by us. The `TODO(D2 spike)` in code is the trigger. **(4) Hidden, or an "answer the red flags to unlock" note? — Split the two states; changed at this review.** A **positive** flag keeps the card hidden: there is nothing to unlock, and an explanatory note there would be actively misleading. An **unanswered** flag now renders the note instead of nothing, because unanswered is the _normal_ state at the start of every single capture — "the card simply is not there" is therefore the state the desk sees most of the time, and it teaches them that panel booking is unreliable, which pushes the booking into Medicus or the Slots tab where none of controls (a)–(m) exist. A one-line sentence carries no button, so none of the automation pull a greyed Book button would, and it makes completing the red-flag screen the visible route to the thing the receptionist wants. Implemented in `bookingGateState()` (`booking-panel-core.js`) and pinned in `test-reception-booking.js`. **Conditions on the deploying organisation:** (i) reception is briefed that this books a **real appointment on the record open in Medicus**, and that the name and DOB at the confirm step are to be **read back to the caller**, not skimmed; (ii) a call that trips a red flag is escalated, never booked — including by hand elsewhere; (iii) sensitive/mental-health calls are never booked from the desk. Any report of a patient-safety incident in which a reception-made booking contributed is treated as a significant safety event and triggers immediate CSO review and suspension of the booking card pending that review.
