| **Description**                 | The Phrases tab (v3.205.0, `side-panel/modules/phrases/phrases.js`) is a personal/practice library of reusable text blocks the clinician composes into one message and **copies**; pasting into a Medicus box and sending remain manual acts in Medicus itself. Five failure modes. (i) **Wrong-context paste** — every block carries an audience (`patient` / `note` / `task`); a patient-facing block pasted into a consultation note is documentation noise, but an internal note or task-comment block pasted into a **patient-facing message** can carry clinical shorthand, blunt working language, or third-party information the patient was never meant to read. (ii) **Unfilled `\***`placeholder sent** — block bodies use`**_`as an Epic-style manual-fill marker (deliberately never auto-filled — see the hard rule below); a message copied and sent with`_**` still in it greets the patient as "Hello \*\*\*", or worse, omits the dose, date or value the instruction depended on. (iii) **Stale shared wording** — a practice-tier block outlives the guidance it encoded (an old call-back number, a superseded safety-net threshold) and is re-sent verbatim for months, with the fluency of canned text lending it false authority. (iv) **Note bloat** — templated paragraphs pasted into consultations degrade the record's signal-to-noise and can read as done-by-template rather than done. (v) **Copy read as sent** (the H-049 automation-bias family) — composing from structured blocks and pressing a button _feels_ like sending; the clinician navigates away believing the patient was told, and nothing was sent anywhere.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Potential causes**            | Automation bias applied to a structured composer (H-007); interruption between Copy and paste-and-send; a block authored with the wrong audience tag, or an LLM-authored block imported and used without review; practice wording never re-reviewed after local guidance changed; habit ("I copied it, so it's handled"); the OS clipboard outliving the patient context it was composed in, so yesterday's message is pasted into today's patient's box (inherent to all clipboard use — the clipboard is OS-level, so the suite cannot scope or clear it; the accepted control is the post-copy status line naming the consequence at the moment of risk: "it stays on the clipboard until you copy something else, so it can land in the wrong patient's box later" — stated where it is read, not mitigated by mechanism). | **Affected users / components** | GPs and practice staff composing patient messages, consultation-note text and task comments — and the patients who read the resulting messages. | **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) **Copy-only by construction** — `composeMessage()` returns a STRING; the module's only output is a clipboard write on an explicit Copy click. No DOM insertion into Medicus, no send, no record write, no fetch. DOM insertion is explicitly a later phase governed by the reception-quick-actions doctrine (CLAUDE.md). (b) **Audience visible at every step** — the audience tag (word + colour, colourblind-safe) renders on every block card AND in the compose preview header; a selection mixing audiences shows a persistent warning naming them ("check every part belongs in the same Medicus box before you paste"); an unknown/invalid audience fails CLOSED to `note` (mislabelling patient text as internal withholds a send; the reverse would invite one). v3.206.1 (design-crit): audience marking on cards/chips is now differential — the expected default ('patient') is unbadged; 'note'/'task' are badged, 'task' in amber — a control at 100% duty cycle had become wallpaper (four identical badges in one 90px band) and trained the eye to skip it. The tray's For:/mixed-audience control — the point where the paste decision is made — is unchanged at full strength. Presentation change only, mechanism untouched; flagged for the pending CSO review. (c) **`\***`is manual-fill only, and the Copy button enforces it** — placeholders are never auto-filled with patient data (hard rule stated in`phrases-core.js`; Accurx deliberately refuses auto-merge for the same reason), they render highlighted in the preview, and Copy with `**\*` remaining demands a second, explicit click whose wording states the **consequence**, not the mechanism — audience-aware, so it is never false for the composition in hand ("the patient will see \*\*\*…" for patient-facing text, "whoever reads this will see \*\*\*…" for notes/tasks; a false consequence teaches click-through-blindness). A `\***`-confirmed copy keeps its obligation visible after the click: the persistent post-copy line appends "This copy still contains \*\*\* — type over every one before you send." (d) **No completion claim** — the post-copy line reads "nothing goes anywhere until you paste and send", persists with no timer until the composition changes, and the words "Done"/"Sent"/"Booked"/"Submitted" never appear in the UI; `test-phrases-core.js`source-greps the module (single-, double-quoted AND template literals, case-insensitively) for the banned claim-words, greps every shipped pack body for completion-claiming phrases, and pins the presence of the`**\*`gate (the`test-reception-quick-actions-ui.js` pattern). (e) **Pack governance** — the shipped pack is validated wholesale in CI (schema, category ids, unique ids, per-block validation), merges are version-gated and tombstoned (a removed practice block stays removed across pack bumps), and changed shipped wording never silently overwrites a practice's stored copy. (f) **Import discipline** — the LLM paste-import validates every block individually with visible per-block rejection reasons; imported blocks land in the personal tier and reach the practice tier only by deliberate promotion; the authoring prompt mandates NHS reading-age 9–11 for patient-audience blocks and forbids patient details, real or invented; backup import whitelist-sanitises every block (`shared/io/phrases-io.js`). (g) **Bloat visibility\*\* — bodies capped at 2000 chars; live character count and an approximate SMS-segment figure at compose time make length a visible property, not a surprise. |

| **Acceptability**               | Accepted (ALARP), **pending CSO review**. The feature automates nothing and claims nothing: it assembles text the clinician was already typing by hand and hands it back through the clipboard, with the manual paste-and-send steps made _more_ visible, not less. The CSO review should focus on: (i) the wording of the curated pack when it replaces the placeholder blocks in `shared/phrases-presets.js` — patient-audience blocks read aloud, safety-netting blocks checked for concrete actions and thresholds; (ii) whether the `***` confirm-gate wording lands with real users or gets click-through-blind (if the latter, escalate to blocking Copy outright while `***` remains); (iii) stale-wording governance — v1 blocks carry **no review-by date** (unlike Knowledge entries); if practice-tier libraries grow, a reviewBy field and a "review due" badge are the follow-up, and that gap is accepted knowingly for a v1 whose shipped pack is centrally curated. ### H-053 / H-054 — recovery note (2026-08-22 clinical-safety audit)

> The two hazard analyses below were drafted on 2026-08-01 by the scheduled weekly change review (commit `2317be2`) but that branch was **never merged** — the register on `main` silently skipped from H-052 to H-055 while both write surfaces (the "Clean up code" widget, CSN W9/W19, and the "Bulk remove?" widget, CSN W10) shipped and remained in the §6.1 inventory. The drafted rows are recovered here verbatim so the register's numbering gap is no longer an undocumented hole; both remain **Proposed — pending CSO review**, exactly as drafted.

### H-053 — "Clean up code" SNOMED replacement suggestions and severity correction: wrong code or wrong significance written to the record

| Field | Value |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Hazard ID** | H-053 |
| **Description** | This week's build-out of the "Clean up code" widget (`content-scripts/problem-description-cleanup.js`, renamed 2026-07-26 from "Fix description", built entirely 2026-07-22 to 2026-07-29 — v3.178.0 through v3.196.0) offers a growing set of one-click coding actions against a patient's active problems, all writing through `POST /clinical/problem/edit-problem/{problemId}`. Four failure modes. (i) **Wrong re-code applied** — the original same-concept relabel (same conceptId, cosmetic wording only) is safety-constrained by construction, but the descendant/laterality (v3.188.0), cross-concept, hint-expanded, confirmed-replacement, and the new POSSIBLY/PARTIALLY EQUIVALENT TO retirement-association candidates (v3.192.0–v3.195.0) are genuine **re-codes to a different SNOMED concept**; SNOMED's own semantics for "partially equivalent" is that the retired concept's meaning is *split* across the offered candidates, so picking one narrows rather than preserves the original meaning. (ii) **Wrong severity written** — the new GP2GP severity-defaulting correction (v3.196.0) parses free-text import boilerplate (`rules/generic-additional-info-text.json`) and offers a one-click "Correct severity to Major/Minor and remove junk text" action that overwrites the structured `significance` field; a mis-tuned regex, an unseen boilerplate layout, or over-generalising the locally-confirmed `PRIORITY=1`→Major mapping to a different source system's own priority scale would write the wrong significance. (iii) **Unconstrained manual search** (v3.189.0) — the manual search box is, in the module's own code comment, "the ONE category with no automated safety constraint at all, functionally identical to typing into Medicus's own Edit Problem search box"; any SNOMED concept can be applied through it. (iv) **Self-reinforcing practice bias** — the new "Cleanup code preferences" (v3.196.0, `shared/preferred-descriptions.js`) offers a practice's own prior wording/remap choices as high-confidence suggestions; a practice's earlier miscoding would resurface as an apparently authoritative precedent for the next similar problem. |
| **Potential causes** | Automation bias applied to a one-click coding tool used many times a day (H-007); a busy clinician clicking through a candidate list without reading the offered wording or the violet "may need reviewing as more than one problem" caution on partially-equivalent candidates; the manual search box's lack of a same-concept constraint being assumed to carry the same safety guarantee as the categories above it; a GP2GP boilerplate layout not yet seen in this practice's data (the pattern set is built incrementally from live examples, most recently confirmed 2026-07-27) causing a false match or a missed one; a source system's severity-scale convention differing from the one confirmed locally. |
| **Affected users / components** | GPs cleaning up coded problem lists, and the patients whose problem-list coding or significance is edited. Components: `content-scripts/problem-description-cleanup.js` (panel UI and all apply paths), `shared/legacy-coded-description.js` (detection heuristic and the same-concept-only filter), `shared/coding-specificity.js` (descendant/laterality extension), `shared/snomed-retirement.js` (REPLACED BY / SAME AS / POSSIBLY / PARTIALLY EQUIVALENT TO resolution), `shared/preferred-descriptions.js` + `shared/io/problem-description-cleanup-io.js` (practice-tier wording/remap learning, Options page), `rules/generic-additional-info-text.json` (GP2GP boilerplate and severity-defaulting patterns). Cross-references **H-007** (automation bias), **H-009** (the v3.203.0 attribute-injection-XSS recurrence in this same feature's Options preferences page — see H-009 control (l)), **H-034** (the same convenience-vs-individual-review balance struck for a different bulk action). |
| **Initial severity** | 4 (Major — a wrong SNOMED re-code or a wrong significance written to a structured field is plausible to contribute to a downstream miscategorisation — e.g. a register/QOF rule or a `requiresProblem`-gated Custom Alert Builder rule keyed on the wrong or now-absent concept — normally caught by the clinician's own review of the candidate before clicking) |
| **Initial likelihood** | 3 (Possible — a fast-moving, opt-in tool used routinely across a busy problem-cleanup session, several of whose categories are genuine re-codes) |
| **Initial risk** | 12 |
| **Controls / mitigations** | (a) **Same-concept-only by construction for the base case** — the original relabel category never offers a different conceptId; "THE SAFETY RULE" is stated as a code comment at the point the candidate list is filtered. (b) **Every genuine re-code shows its candidate wording and concept before the click** — no category pre-fills or auto-applies; each suggestion renders as its own labelled button/lozenge. (c) **PARTIALLY EQUIVALENT TO renders with a distinct violet banner and explicit caution copy** ("this record may need reviewing as more than one problem"), never styled or grouped as if it were a same-confidence-tier suggestion. (d) **One lozenge per SNOMED code, not one per synonym** (v3.195.0) — a code with several wordings collapses to one code-level decision plus a wording `<select>`, so the clinician is not shown what looks like several different alternatives for what is actually one coding choice. (e) **The unconstrained manual search is visually and textually distinguished** — neutral grey styling, explicitly separated from the risk-graded categories above it, with copy stating plainly there is no automated check. (f) **Severity correction shows its source and requires an explicit click per problem** — the offered value, its source import text, and an explanation are rendered before the "Correct severity…" button; `applyCorrectSeverityAndRemoveJunk` only fires on that click, never automatically, and only ever raises the question for the clinician to confirm, not silently. (g) **`PRIORITY=n` values with no confirmed mapping render an informational review note only, no button** — the mechanism explicitly distinguishes a confident, locally-confirmed correction from a merely-observed pattern, and defaults to the conservative (no-action) path when confidence is not established. (h) **Preferences are suggestion-only and manually overridable** — `pdc.preferredDescriptions` / `pdc.conceptRemap` are never auto-applied; a clinician can set/clear a manual override per concept on the Options page, and tallying continues visibly underneath it so a practice can check whether the pinned choice is still the one being used. (i) **Generic-import-text removal is surgical, span-based, and separately styled plain** — it strips only the exact matched boilerplate substring, never a whole line or field, and genuine free text sharing a line with boilerplate is preserved (`test-problem-description-cleanup.js`). (j) **Reassurance note when the code itself is not in question** (v3.196.0) — a problem flagged only for import-text housekeeping is explicitly told its own SNOMED code is not flagged as outdated or retired, so the suggestion wall below is not misread as "the code is wrong." (k) **API errors now surface the server's real reason** (v3.196.0), so a rejected write is self-diagnosing rather than silently retried or misread as success. (l) **Wrong-patient discipline** (v3.203.0) — the clinical-summary scan discards a stale response if the clinician has switched patients before it lands, so a slow fetch cannot match candidates against the wrong patient's DOM. (m) 276+ automated checks across `test-snomed-retirement.js` and `test-problem-description-cleanup.js` regression-guard the detection heuristics, the same-concept filter, the severity-parsing patterns and the API payload shapes. |
| **Residual severity** | 4 |
| **Residual likelihood** | 2 (Unlikely — the highest-risk paths (re-codes, severity correction) all require an explicit per-instance click against visible candidate wording, and the base relabel path cannot re-code at all; residual risk sits mainly in the unconstrained manual-search category and in whether a busy clinician reads the candidate before clicking, which no UI control fully eliminates) |
| **Residual risk** | 8 — Acceptable with documented controls (ALARP), **pending CSO review** |
| **Acceptability** | Accepted (ALARP), **pending CSO review** — this hazard was not previously recorded; the feature was built and shipped (v3.178.0–v3.196.0) without a corresponding hazard-log entry until this sync. The CSO review should focus on: (i) whether the manual-search category (no automated safety constraint) needs its own explicit on-screen warning beyond the neutral styling; (ii) whether PARTIALLY/POSSIBLY EQUIVALENT TO candidates should require a stronger confirmation step than the other re-code categories, given SNOMED's own "split meaning" semantics; (iii) whether the `PRIORITY=1`→Major mapping, confirmed against one source system's convention, should be scoped/labelled more explicitly so it is not read as a general rule; (iv) whether downstream `requiresProblem`-gated rules (Custom Alert Builder, QOF registers) should be considered when a problem's conceptId changes via this tool, in case a register-defining code is inadvertently re-coded out of its register. |

### H-054 — "Bulk remove?" batch-ending of active problems against the wrong problem, or with unnoticed downstream effect on register/monitoring rules

| Field | Value |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Hazard ID** | H-054 |
| **Description** | `content-scripts/problem-bulk-end.js` (built 2026-07-24 to 2026-07-27 across v3.181.0–v3.195.0, converged into one "Bulk remove?" widget v3.194.0) injects a checkbox inline next to every active problem in the Clinical Summary list; ticked rows are ended in one batch via `POST /clinical/problem/end-problem` — a genuine, immediate, per-row write to Medicus with no per-instance Medicus confirmation dialog. Three failure modes. (i) **Wrong problem ticked and ended** in a long checklist, under time pressure, or by mistaking "end" for "not clinically significant" rather than "no longer active." (ii) **The "Select flagged" convenience mis-scopes** — it auto-ticks only rows the SNOMED admin/non-clinical-root badge scan flags as clean (uncautioned), but the 18 non-problem roots added this week (v3.191.0) were researched via the public NHS terminology API only and re-confirmed against Medicus's own live search rather than against a real patient's coded problem end-to-end, so a root's scope could in principle be broader in practice than intended. (iii) **Downstream register/monitoring suppression** — ending a problem removes it from the active list that the suite's own rules engine reads for `requiresProblem`/`requiresAnyProblem`-gated Custom Alert Builder rules and QOF register logic (H-002, H-016); a wrongly-ended problem (e.g. a chronic-disease register code) would silently stop firing the drug-monitoring, QOF-recall or PINCER-style alerts that depend on its presence across Sentinel, Sweep and the Signing Queue, with nothing in this widget's own UI surfacing that connection at the point of ending. |
| **Potential causes** | A long problem list with many checkboxes inviting a fast, low-attention pass; "ending" read as low-consequence because the code stays in the record; the badge scan's caution-attribution failing to distinguish a genuinely admin code from a superficially similar clinical one for a root not yet tested against real patient data; a clinician not connecting "this ends the problem" with "this also silences every rule gated on this problem being present," because that link exists only in the rules engine, not in this widget's own copy. |
| **Affected users / components** | GPs batch-tidying problem lists, and the patients whose active problem list — and any Sentinel/Sweep/Signing-Queue rule gated on it — is changed. Components: `content-scripts/problem-bulk-end.js` (checklist, confirm summary, POST), `rules/non-problem-root-codes.json` (badge-scan roots), the retired `content-scripts/problem-junk-code-cleanup.js` whose pure helpers now live in the file above. Cross-references **H-002** (missing alert — a rule that stops firing because its gating problem was removed), **H-016** (PINCER false-negative, same class), **H-034** ("Select all" bulk-selects the wrong or too many items — the same convenience-vs-review tension applied here to a harder-to-reverse action: ending a problem, not ticking a checkbox in another system). |
| **Initial severity** | 4 (Major — wrongly ending an active problem is itself a moderate direct harm, but the plausible downstream effect of silencing a register- or monitoring-gated rule this suite itself relies on is a missed-monitoring scenario normally intercepted by other controls) |
| **Initial likelihood** | 3 (Possible — a batch UI over a list of many checkboxes, used during routine list-tidying) |
| **Initial risk** | 12 |
| **Controls / mitigations** | (a) **Nothing is ever pre-ticked, and there is no blanket "select all"** — every problem must be individually reviewed and ticked; the one convenience, "Select flagged," ticks only rows flagged admin/non-clinical AND carrying no caution — a row whose caution attribution errored is treated as cautioned, never as clean (fail closed). (b) **Dependent problems are hard-excluded, not just warned about** — a problem whose end-problem form reports active child problems has its checkbox disabled by `isEndable`. (c) **Two-step confirm with an explicit ENDING/KEEPING summary** — "Review selected" renders the full ending list and the full kept list before any POST; only the Confirm button on that summary submits, per the duplicate-checker's house pattern for record-changing actions. (d) **End date and reason are guarded at both layers** — the buttons disable without them, and `endSelected()` independently refuses to POST regardless of button state, so an empty end date or blank reason can never reach the record. (e) **Ending is end-dating, not deletion** — the code and history remain in the record; the confirm copy states this plainly, though the record is removed from the *active* list read by this suite's own rules engine (see Description (iii)). (f) **No auto-reload after success** — a manual "Refresh page" link is offered instead, so an in-progress consultation is never lost to an unrequested reload. (g) **Per-batch audit trail** — every successful batch is recorded in the local Clinical Event Ledger (patient UUID + action only; the free-typed reason is never written to the ledger). (h) **Failed POSTs surface the server's actual response body per row**, never a bare status code. (i) **Inline-injection discipline followed** — prepend-only, re-injected on every SPA mutation tick, state keyed by problem id so a Vue re-render never silently loses a tick (per the CLAUDE.md queue-chip doctrine this widget explicitly follows). |
| **Residual severity** | 4 |
| **Residual likelihood** | 1 (Rare — the two-step confirm with a read-back ENDING/KEEPING summary, the absence of any pre-ticking or blanket select-all, the hard exclusion of problems with active children, and the double-layer date/reason guard together make an un-reviewed batch end very unlikely; the downstream register/monitoring-suppression failure mode (iii) is not separately controlled by this widget and is the residual risk this score carries) |
| **Residual risk** | 4 — Acceptable (ALARP), **pending CSO review** |
| **Acceptability** | Accepted (ALARP), **pending CSO review** — this hazard was not previously recorded; the widget's own code comments record an informal "SAFETY POSTURE (CSO review 2026-07-26)" design review that shaped the two-step confirm and fail-closed "Select flagged" behaviour, but no corresponding entry existed in this hazard log until this sync, so that review has not previously been captured as a numbered, scored hazard. The CSO review should confirm: (i) the design decisions already reflected in code (fail-closed caution attribution, hard child-problem exclusion, no blanket select-all) as adequate; (ii) whether the widget's confirm-summary copy should name the register/monitoring-suppression risk (iii) explicitly, given it is not obvious from the widget's own UI that ending a problem can silence a rule elsewhere in the suite; (iii) whether the 18 non-problem roots added v3.191.0 need live-patient re-confirmation before "Select flagged" is treated as low-risk in practice, not just in principle. |

| **Description**                 | The Contacts Management canvas (v3.208.0, `content-scripts/contacts-canvas.js`) converts a patient's manual, free-text contacts into REAL patient-to-patient links in Medicus, and every one of those actions is a genuine write on two records at once: the forward relationship on the index patient (`POST /patient/patient-contact/link-patient`), the reverse relationship written onto the CANDIDATE's own record (a second, separate POST), a re-categorisation of an existing link (`change-patient-contact`), a relationship deletion (`delete-patient-contact-relationship`), and a bulk import of another patient's contact set (`link-contacts`, `content-scripts/contacts-link-button.js`). Four routes to a wrong-person link. (i) **Match badge steers to the wrong household member** — candidates are scored and badged strong/possible/weak (`engine/contact-match.js`); in a same-surname household several real patients score alike, and a "strong" badge against the wrong sibling, parent or child is an invitation to drag them onto the slot. (ii) **The reciprocal write lands on another patient's record** — the reverse link is written onto the candidate, who is not the record on screen; if the candidate is the wrong person, a stranger's record gains a next-of-kin / copy-correspondence relationship to a patient they have nothing to do with. (iii) **Bulk-import misclassification** — `link-contacts` is a BLIND copy of a source patient's contact rows (confirmed live: it preserves whatever the source row already was), and relationship free text that does not parse lands as `other`, so a household's contacts can be attached wholesale with relationships that were never true of this patient. (iv) **Wrong deletion** — the canvas deletes relationship records (the merged manual duplicate, a blank import artefact, and a best-effort "reverse manual match" found on the candidate's own record). None of this is cosmetic: `patientContactIsNextOfKin` and `patientContactCopyCorrespondence` decide who the practice rings in an emergency and who may lawfully receive correspondence about this patient.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Potential causes**            | Two or more registered patients at one address sharing a surname (and often a first name), with a manual contact recorded as a surname only or as "Mum"; free text that names a THIRD party's relative ("Son's wife") or that parses to a relationship the GP did not mean; a double-click firing the link POST twice (the endpoint has no idempotency guard — a repeat creates a genuine second relationship, confirmed live); a multi-step write failing between the forward and the reverse POST and being retried from the start; an SPA navigation to a different patient between opening the canvas and pressing Confirm (the H-043 race); automation bias applied to a structured, confidently-badged suggestion list (H-007); GP2GP-imported manual contacts naming people who are not registered at this practice at all; a bulk import taken from a source patient whose own contact list was itself wrong. | **Affected users / components** | GPs and administrative staff doing contact-hygiene work, and BOTH patients on either end of every link. Components: `content-scripts/contacts-canvas.js` (`buildConfirmForCard`, `tryAssign`, `doCanvasConfirm`, `confirmMerge`, `deleteBlankManualContact`, the reverse-manual removal handler in `bindEvents`), `content-scripts/contacts-api.js` (`performLinkAndCleanup` — the single shared write orchestration carrying the wrong-patient guard — plus `findReverseManualMatch`), `content-scripts/contacts-link-button.js` (`pickImportSource`, `doImportConfirm`), `engine/contact-match.js` (`scoreCandidate`, `rankCandidates`, `nameSearchQueries`), `engine/contact-relationships.js` (`normaliseFreeText`, `isPossessiveConstruction`, `invertRelationship`, `composeViaHub`, `findExistingForwardLink`/`findExistingReciprocal`), `engine/contact-tree.js` (`commitSuggestion`, `assignToSlot`/`removeFromSlot`), `rules/contact-relationships.json`. discipline is the model for this one), **H-007** (automation bias), **H-029** (a captured draft restored against the wrong contact) and **H-047** (the same wrong-person-attribution concern in a read-only surface).                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) **Nothing is ever auto-applied, at any score** — every conversion is human-confirmed by dragging the candidate onto a named slot and then pressing Confirm; `commitSuggestion()` is structurally the ONLY path from a suggestion into a committed edge (`engine/contact-tree.js`, pinned in `test-contact-tree.js` §2), so "never link something the user has not explicitly confirmed on screen" is a property of the module's API surface rather than a UI convention. (b) **Scores rank, they do not decide, and the weakest signals cannot dominate** — `WEIGHTS` in `engine/contact-match.js` is name 55 / address 20 / age 8 / gender 7 / phone 5 / email 5; a gender or age mismatch is a shrug (0.5), never a filter, because a shared family email and a child's record carrying a parent's mobile are known local patterns; `test-contact-match.js` §3–§5 pin that phone/email cannot rescue a poor name match and that a mismatch costs only its own component. (c) **Name matching is token-granular, not substring** — `tokenContainment` requires whole-token containment with at least `MIN_CONTAINMENT_TOKENS` (2) on the shorter side, so a surname-only manual entry no longer buys every same-surname person at the address the 0.9 containment tier (and, with the same-address bonus, a "strong" badge for what is really "someone in that household"); it falls to the Jaccard band and is visibly a weaker claim. Pinned in `test-contact-match.js` §1a/§1a(ii), including the 'Ann' inside 'Annette' and surname-only-plus-same-address regressions. (d) **Ambiguity is signalled, not hidden** — `rankCandidates()` marks the top result `tied` when the runner-up is within `TIE_MARGIN` (5, the weight of the single weakest signal, i.e. the ordering was decided by exactly one signal the GP said must never be decisive), and reports `margin: null` rather than 0 when there is no runner-up so "not measurable" can never be read as "a close call"; pinned in `test-contact-match.js` §7. (e) **Same-name collisions are disambiguated on screen** — `loadCanvas` flags only those candidate names mapping to more than one distinct patient id, and `disambiguationSuffix()` appends address/phone/email for exactly those cards (or states plainly that none is on record); every card also shows the patient's age in brackets. (f) **Free text fails closed to needs-review, never to a guess** — `normaliseFreeText()` matches the WHOLE string against a canonical label or a shipped alias (never a per-word scan: "Carer for his mother" is not a mother), and `isPossessiveConstruction()` rejects a third party's relative outright ("Son's wife" previously returned `wife` at 0.85 and would have pre-filled that onto a real write); an unmatched contact is coloured needs-review with no relationship pre-filled. Pinned in `test-contact-relationships.js` §2/§5. (g) **Composition is deliberately narrow** — `composeViaHub()` pre-fills only the structurally unconditional grandparent/in-law hops through UNMODIFIED parent/child/partner edges, and returns null for everything else (either hop carrying Step-/Half-/Ex-, sibling-via-one-parent, step-parent via a partner hop), so an uncertain hop is never compounded into a confident label; whatever it does propose remains an editable field in the confirm panel. Pinned in `test-contact-relationships.js` §4b. (h) **One wrong-patient guard, in the shared write path** — `performLinkAndCleanup()` (`contacts-api.js`) re-derives the live page's identity via `resolveContext()` and aborts before ANY write if it no longer matches the `patientId` pinned when the user opened the confirm action; it lives there once precisely so a second UI surface cannot implement it differently. `doImportConfirm()` and `mergeDuplicateAddressGroup()` repeat the same re-verify for their own writes. All identity is UUID-based throughout — no write is ever keyed on a name. (i) **Duplicate links are prevented rather than error-handled, and a double-click cannot write twice** — `findExistingForwardLink`/`findExistingReciprocal` are consulted before the forward and reverse writes respectively (POST `link-patient` has no idempotency guard: a repeat creates a real second relationship, and a duplicate forward is rejected 400), and every link/delete control is busy-guarded for the lifetime of its in-flight request (the per-id `phoneDeleting`/`phoneFixingType`/`addressMerging` sets and the equivalent busy flag on the Confirm-link, merge-finalise and remove-manual buttons). (j) **The multi-step write is resumable** — the forward → reverse → manual-delete sequence records what has already succeeded, so a failure part-way is retried from where it stopped instead of re-firing an already-created forward link, and the on-screen error states that nothing further was changed. (k) **Both writes are stated in words before either fires** — the confirm panel is two columns: what will be recorded on the index patient's record, and what will be written onto the candidate's OWN record, with each next-of-kin / copy-correspondence tick spelled out as a sentence ("This will allow messages to be sent to X about Y"). The reverse label is never independently chosen — always the gender-aware inversion (`invertRelationship`) — and an inversion that is ambiguous suggests nothing at all rather than guessing. (l) **Deletion is bounded and never speculative** — the only relationship records deleted are the manual duplicate the human has just declared to be the same person, a blank (no name, no relationship) import artefact behind its own explicit Delete, and the reverse manual match, which is OFFERED and never taken automatically (`findReverseManualMatch` is best-effort, returns null below a 0.6 name score, and its full detail is shown side-by-side as comparison evidence before the human decides). (m) **Bulk import is a filtered, per-row decision** — `pickImportSource()` drops rows with no real patient behind them and rows already linked to this patient (counting both back to the user), then shows each remaining row with its source relationship text, an editable relationship picker and next-of-kin / copy-correspondence ticks defaulting OFF; only the rows explicitly ticked are sent, and unparsed relationship text lands as `other` rather than as a guessed category. (n) **Nothing in the clinical record proper is touched** — no problem, medication, observation, task or appointment is written by this feature; its entire write surface is the patient-contact/address/telephone demographic set, reached only from a record the user already has open and authenticated against. |

| **Acceptability**               | **Accepted (ALARP) — CSO REVIEWED AND SIGNED OFF 2026-08-01.** Signed off: Dr D. Triska (CSO), recorded via session instruction ("Read and signed"), 2026-08-01 (chat). The honest comparison is not "linking versus no linking" but "linking through this canvas versus the same user doing it by hand in Medicus": on every identity axis the canvas is the stricter of the two (Medicus offers no candidate ranking, no tie signal, no same-name disambiguation, no duplicate-link pre-check and no commit-time re-verification), and the axis on which it is weaker — that a ranked list makes a wrong candidate easy to accept — is what controls (b)–(e) exist for. The pre-merge review of this PR closed the four gaps that mattered most here (token-granular containment replacing surname-only "strong" badges, tie/ambiguity signalling, possessive free text failing closed to needs-review, and double-click/busy guards plus a resumable multi-step write) and they are pinned in CI. Questions recorded at proposal, carried forward as open review items (not conditions of this sign-off): (i) whether the word "strong" survives contact with a real same-surname household or should be re-worded to something that cannot be read as an identification; (ii) whether the reverse column's next-of-kin / copy-correspondence ticks — which write onto a patient NOT on screen — warrant a second, explicit confirmation of their own; (iii) whether bulk import (`link-contacts`, a blind copy of another patient's contact rows) belongs in a first release at all, or should ship disabled pending a review of what practices actually import; and (iv) whether a wrong link, once written, is straightforward for a practice to unpick in Medicus. Any report of a link, re-categorisation or deletion landing on the wrong person is to be treated as a significant safety event, triggering immediate CSO review and suspension of the write paths pending that review. | **Description**                 | Alongside relationship linking, the contacts canvas performs **demographic hygiene writes on real records**, and both are destructive rather than additive. (i) **Duplicate-address merge** on the index patient: PDS re-sends the same address in different shapes, so the canvas groups likely duplicates (`findDuplicateAddressGroups`) and, on one click, DELETES every member of the group except the one kept (`delete-address`) and rewrites the correspondence-address flag onto the survivor (`change-address`, a full-replace write). Two ways this loses real data — grouping two genuinely DIFFERENT addresses (a neighbouring house, another flat in the same building) and deleting one of them; or deleting the copy that held `isCorrespondenceAddress` without moving that flag, after which the practice's letters go to the wrong place with nothing on screen to say so. (ii) **Phone edit / delete / "Fix type"** on the CANDIDATE's own record (`change-telephone-number`, `delete-telephone-number`): these edit a second patient's registered demographic data from inside the index patient's canvas, and `change-telephone-number` is a full replace, not a patch, so any field not sent back is silently wiped. Deleting the number a patient is actually reachable on, or wiping its `preferredTelephoneNumberForSms` flag or its notes, degrades the practice's ability to contact them — an appointment, a result, a safety-netting call — and nothing in the suite would surface that it had happened.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Potential causes**            | Two distinct addresses at one postcode sharing their house/flat numbering; a one-click destructive action reached through a panel the user has stopped reading (H-007 automation bias, sharpened by the deliberate "the visible context IS the confirmation" convention — no separate popup); a transient API failure while reading a member's correspondence-address status, leaving the flag's true owner unknown; a stale in-memory copy of the phone list used to build a full-replace body; a phone action fired against a merge that has already moved on to a different candidate; a double-click issuing a second delete; the user assuming an address or number can be restored afterwards when it cannot. | **Affected users / components** | GPs and administrative staff doing contact hygiene, the index patient, and any linked contact whose own phone record is edited from this canvas. Pinned by `test-contact-relationships.js` §10–§12. | **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) **The duplicate test is conservative by design, because a false positive deletes a real address** — `isLikelyDuplicateAddress()` requires BOTH addresses to carry a postcode and for it to match once normalised (never text similarity alone), requires their NUMERIC tokens (house/flat numbers) to match EXACTLY rather than merely overlap — a differing number is never noise, it is what distinguishes one real address from its neighbour — and only then requires heavy word-token overlap (`DUPLICATE_TOKEN_THRESHOLD` 0.7); a missing or blank postcode on either side is never a duplicate. Pinned, including the "Flat 1 vs Flat 2 at one postcode" and field-boundary cases, in `test-contact-relationships.js` §10. (b) **Scope is the hub patient only** — the caller only ever passes the index patient's OWN `patientAddressSection.patientAddresses`; a linked contact's addresses are never grouped or merged. (c) **The survivor is a default, not a decision** — `chooseAddressToKeep()` prefers the correspondence address above all else, then the most complete record, then a deterministic first-in-order tiebreak; the panel then shows EVERY address in the group in full text with radio buttons, notes which one currently holds the correspondence flag, and lets the GP override the default before merging. (d) **Fail-closed when the correspondence flag cannot be verified** — `isCorrespondenceAddress` is only reachable per-address (`getEditAddress`), and an empty detail object is indistinguishable from a verified "not the correspondence address"; a member that cannot be read (fetch failure, or no `addressId` at all) is recorded in `unverifiedIndexes`, the group is still SHOWN with the unverifiable member marked "couldn't be checked", and its Merge control is disabled with an explicit note — with `mergeDuplicateAddressGroup()` re-checking the same condition itself so the refusal never rests on a `disabled` attribute alone. (e) **The flag is transferred BEFORE anything is deleted** — when the GP keeps an address other than the one holding the correspondence designation, `buildChangeAddressBody()` writes that designation onto the survivor first, so an interruption or a failure part-way through the sequence can never leave the patient with no correspondence address; the body is a full replace built from the kept address's own fields plus its already-fetched description/access notes, so nothing else on that record is altered. Pinned in `test-contact-relationships.js` §11–§12. (f) **The wrong-patient guard applies to these writes too** — `mergeDuplicateAddressGroup()` re-derives the page's identity via `resolveContext()` and aborts before the first delete if it no longer matches the pinned `patientId`, and every step re-checks that the canvas state instance has not been replaced (`if (st !== cs) return`). (g) **Phone actions are entry-scoped and re-verified against the merge they belong to** — every phone action carries the specific `telephoneNumberId` (never "the Home number" generically, so a patient with several is safe by construction) AND the candidate id it was opened for; `savePhoneEdit`, `deletePhoneNumber` and `fixPhoneType` all refuse to write if the merge has moved on to a different candidate ("reopen the edit to try again"), which is the wrong-patient guard in its write-target form. (h) **Full-replace writes are built from a fresh read, never from cached state** — `fixPhoneType` re-fetches `getEditTelephoneNumber` and sends back the number, preferred-for-SMS flag and notes exactly as currently recorded, changing only the type, and resolves the type's write value from the authoritative `telephoneNumberTypes` list on that same response rather than assuming a label; it aborts with "nothing was changed" if no valid option is found. Every phone write is followed by a re-fetch rather than a local patch, so the panel always shows what Medicus actually holds. (i) **Concurrent and repeated clicks cannot double-fire** — in-flight phone and address actions are tracked per id/group (`phoneDeleting`, `phoneFixingType`, `addressMerging` sets, not single flags), the affected controls render disabled and busy while the request is outstanding, and the panel disables the whole group's radios and Merge control mid-merge. (j) **The claim made on screen is a data-quality observation, never a clinical one** — the "looks like a mobile filed as Home" warning rests on a structural fact about UK numbering (`isUkMobileNumber`, Ofcom's 07 range, pinned in `test-contact-relationships.js` §9), not on inference about the patient; and the phone-note warning ("mum's mobile") is surfaced verbatim from the record rather than interpreted. |

| **Description**                 | The contacts canvas necessarily brings a SECOND patient's identifiable data onto the record of a FIRST. Two distinct exposures. (i) **Shared contact-info flagging (confidentiality)** — to catch the known local pattern of a child's record carrying a parent's own mobile or email, the canvas compares the index patient's non-Home phone/email against a linked contact's and, on a match, badges the card "Shares contact info" and prints the shared number or address, plus a hint about whose it looks like, INSIDE the index patient's canvas. Candidate cards likewise carry a name, age, and — for same-name collisions — an address, phone or email belonging to another patient. Misread, the flag can also be taken as a verdict about who the number belongs to rather than the detection-only signal it is, and acted on by deleting a number that was correct. (ii) **A family graph persisted at rest** — the "Next family member" cycling flow survives a real browser navigation by writing the session (patient UUIDs, the pending/visited pools and the committed relationship edges — i.e. a machine-readable map of who is related to whom) to `chrome.storage.local` under `contactsCanvas.familySession`. On a shared clinical workstation, a session left behind is a small family graph sitting on disk after the consultation that created it has ended, and, if it were ever swept into a suite backup, would be restorable onto another machine whose user has no business seeing it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Potential causes**            | A canvas left open, or a cycling session abandoned mid-review, on a shared desktop; a family graph written to storage with no expiry or no pruning; a new storage key silently missed by the backup-coverage guard and swept into a suite export (the exact drift `CLAUDE.md` records as the reason the IO files own the backup contract); a shared-contact-info flag read as an assertion of ownership rather than as a prompt to check; a third party's contact detail shown on a card being copied into the wrong patient's record; a household sharing one genuine landline or inbox generating routine flags that train the eye to ignore the real ones (H-012 alert fatigue).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **Affected users / components** | The index patient, every linked contact whose details are surfaced, and the clinicians reading the canvas. Components: `findSharedContactInfo`/`emailOwnerHint`/`isHomeType` in `engine/contact-relationships.js`; `sharedContactInfoDetailHtml`, `cardHtml`, `disambiguationSuffix`, and the "Family cycling" section (`FAMILY_SESSION_STORAGE_KEY`, `FAMILY_SESSION_MAX_AGE_MS`, `persistFamilySession`, `loadPersistedFamilySession`, `clearPersistedFamilySession`, `checkResumableFamilySession`) in `content-scripts/contacts-canvas.js`; `dobSortValue`/`createFamilySession` in `engine/contact-tree.js`; the backup exclusion in `test-backup-coverage.js`. Pinned by `test-contact-relationships.js` §13 and `test-contact-tree.js` §5/§7. Cross-references **H-009** (patient data egress — nothing here leaves the browser), **H-047** (a device-local, never-backed-up ledger holding patient UUIDs, the same doctrine applied to a rolling contact log) and **H-012** (alert fatigue from a flag that fires on ordinary household sharing). data-minimisation concern rather than an egress or a wrong-treatment one) | **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) **No data leaves the browser** — every fetch is a same-origin, credentialed call to Medicus's own endpoints from a content script that already shares the page's session; there is no extension backend, no third-party call and no telemetry on this path (H-009's boundary, unchanged by this feature). (b) **The shared-info check is detection-only and never resolves ownership** — `findSharedContactInfo()` reports what is shared and offers `emailOwnerHint` as an explicitly non-decisive hint that returns null on any tie rather than guessing; nothing is deleted or rewritten on the strength of it, and the card's own age display is what lets the clinician judge (a 7-year-old with "their own" mobile). (c) **Ordinary household sharing is excluded by design** — Home-type phones AND Home-type emails are excluded on both sides, so a shared household landline or inbox does not fire the flag; this keeps the signal rare enough to remain worth reading (H-012). Pinned in `test-contact-relationships.js` §13. (d) **The stored session is minimised to what cycling actually needs** — patient UUIDs, a visited/pending set and committed edges; names never enter the engine's session shape at all (only a display-only `targetName` in the storage wrapper), and a date of birth is converted to a plain ordering value at the boundary (`dobSortValue`) so no date of birth is ever written to disk (`engine/contact-tree.js`). (e) **The session is short-lived and eagerly pruned** — `FAMILY_SESSION_MAX_AGE_MS` is 4 hours, and `checkResumableFamilySession()` calls the loader unconditionally on EVERY Medicus page load, so an expired session is deleted on the next page view of any kind rather than only if the user happens to return to the record cycling was heading for; the resume banner is only ever offered when the page's own patient is exactly the session's target, and Dismiss clears the key. Resuming consumes and clears the stored copy. (f) **Never backed up, and CI-guarded that way** — `contactsCanvas.familySession` is listed as a deliberate, documented backup exclusion in `test-backup-coverage.js` (with the `contactsCanvas` prefix added to the scanner's own key-prefix list, so the drift guard can actually see the key rather than silently filtering it out); restoring a mid-review family graph onto another machine days later is exactly the outcome the exclusion prevents. (g) **The cycling flow is opt-in and never silently moves the user** — advancing to another family member requires an explicit named confirmation ("This will leave <patient>'s record and open <name>'s own record…"), and the resume prompt is a small dismissible banner rather than an overlay that reopens itself over whoever is now on screen. (h) **Everything rendered is escaped** — `esc()` is applied to every name, relationship, phone, email and address string rendered into the canvas, so record free text cannot inject markup into the page. |

### H-058 — Staffing decision taken on a stale or degraded rota status panel

| Field                           | Value |
| ------------------------------- | ----- |
| **Hazard ID**                   | H-058 |
| **Description**                 | The compact **Rota** module (v3.211.0) shows today's duty cover, who is on leave, sessions still needing cover, and this week's high-priority safe-staffing warnings. A manager or duty clinician takes a **staffing decision** (leaves a session uncovered, does not call a locum, does not escalate a supervision gap) on the basis of a panel that is **stale** (data changed elsewhere since the panel last refreshed) or **degraded** (the pure rules engine could not evaluate the stored rota, so no check actually ran). The safety-relevant failure mode is the degraded one: absence of a check rendering as absence of a problem. |
| **Potential causes**            | Malformed stored rota data makes `rota/engine/rules.js` throw (e.g. a `rota.settings` with a null `openDays`), so `checkWeek`/`capacitySummary` produce nothing; the panel is left open across a date change or a colleague edits the rota on another machine; the compact module is read as the source of truth instead of the full application; the rota was never fully populated, so a check has nothing to fire on. |
| **Affected users / components** | Practice managers, rota administrators and duty clinicians. Components: `side-panel/modules/rota/rota.js` (compact module in the side panel and pop-out), `rota/engine/rules.js`, `rota/shared/store.js`. |
| **Initial severity**            | 3 (Moderate — a staffing shortfall that the practice's own duty/escalation processes would normally intercept; the hazard is organisational, mediated by human decision, and no patient-specific output is produced) |
| **Initial likelihood**          | 3 (Possible — malformed stored data and cross-machine edits both occur in normal use) |
| **Initial risk**                | 9 |
| **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) **Explicit degraded state (v3.211.0 review fix).** When the engine throws, the module tracks the failure and renders an **amber** "Safe-staffing checks unavailable — open the full rota to investigate" card. It never renders the green "None" that a swallowed exception previously produced, and the capacity figure is suppressed rather than shown as zero. (b) **No positive assertion from a failed computation.** In the degraded state the duty pills degrade from green "OK" to a neutral "Unchecked", and "Sessions needing cover — None outstanding" becomes "Not verified — check the full rota". A **Gap** is still shown in red: a degraded state never hides a problem, it only withdraws reassurance. (c) **The full application is the stated source of truth**; the compact module is explicitly a glance and carries a button (and an "Opens in a new tab" hint) into it. (d) **Warn-never-block posture**: the rota's safe-staffing rules encode BMA/CQC/NHSE **guidance**, not law; the panel footer states this, thresholds are practice settings, and the software never prevents a staffing arrangement. (e) The module refreshes on `chrome.storage.onChanged` for `rota.*` and polls once a minute so a panel left open overnight rolls the date over. (f) `rota/shared/store.js` coerces the settings members the engine dereferences back to their shipped defaults when a stored value is not an array, so the commonest cause of the degraded state cannot persist silently. (g) No patient-identifiable data is read or persisted by the module, so no wrong-patient pathway exists. |
| **Residual severity**           | 3 |
| **Residual likelihood**         | 2 |
| **Residual risk**               | 6 — Acceptable (ALARP) |
| **Acceptability**               | Accepted (ALARP). The explicit unavailable state is the primary control: the panel now fails loud and amber rather than quietly green. Residual risk is the ordinary organisational risk of acting on a summary view, mitigated by the full application being the source of truth and by the warn-never-block design. |
