### H-059 — Malformed shared-drive sync data corrupts rota state

| Field                           | Value |
| ------------------------------- | ----- |
| **Hazard ID**                   | H-059 |
| **Description**                 | The rota can optionally replicate itself through a single JSON file in a folder on the practice's shared drive (`rota/shared/sync.js`), re-read every 15 seconds, read-modify-write, last-writer-wins. A **malformed, truncated or tampered** document — that folder is writable by anyone with access to the share — is read back and applied, corrupting the locally stored rota: staffing information is lost, replaced or made unreadable, or the rules engine begins to throw on every render (see H-058), and the practice's view of who is working becomes wrong. |
| **Potential causes**            | A partially-written file caught mid-write by the 15-second poll; a hand-edited or third-party-generated file; a wrong file dropped in the folder; a future/older schema; deliberate tampering by anyone with write access to the share; a concurrent edit lost to last-writer-wins. |
| **Affected users / components** | Practice managers, rota administrators and all staff whose sessions the rota describes. Components: `rota/shared/sync.js`, `rota/app/app.js` (`applyRemote`), `rota/shared/store.js`, `rota/engine/validate.js`. |
| **Initial severity**            | 3 (Moderate — corrupted staffing information leading to an uncovered or wrongly-covered session; organisational, mediated by human decision, no patient-specific output) |
| **Initial likelihood**          | 3 (Possible — an unauthenticated, shared, last-writer-wins file re-read every 15 seconds is not a trusted input) |
| **Initial risk**                | 9 |
| **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) **Validation on the read-back path (v3.211.0 review fix).** `rota/engine/validate.js` (`validateRotaScopes`) type-checks all eight `rota.*` scopes — arrays and their elements, the demand day-map, and the `rota.settings` members the engine dereferences — and `applyRemote` calls it **before writing anything**. Previously the hot sync path saved remote scopes verbatim while only the cold backup path validated. (b) **Refuse whole, never partially apply.** A document with any rejected scope is discarded in full; the local rota is left untouched rather than half-overwritten. (c) **Never silent.** The rejection raises the same toast used for a failed sync push, plus a sticky banner in Settings naming the version, the author and the reasons — a pulled version is only ever returned once, so a transient toast alone could be the sole notice. (d) **Belt-and-braces coercion** in `rota/shared/store.js`: settings array members that are not arrays fall back to the shipped defaults on load, so already-stored bad data cannot crash the engine. (e) **Parity test** `test-rota-validate.js` feeds identical malformed fixtures to both the sync validator and the backup-import validator (`shared/io/rota-io.js`) and asserts both reject each one, so the two independent copies of the checks cannot drift apart. (f) Sync is **opt-in**, requires an explicit per-machine folder grant, and the file never leaves the practice's own storage (see `docs/DPIA.md`). (g) The version counter is monotonic and pushes are read-modify-write, so an older document never overwrites a newer one. |
| **Residual severity**           | 3 |
| **Residual likelihood**         | 1 |
| **Residual risk**               | 3 — Broadly acceptable |
| **Acceptability**               | Accepted. Validate-before-write with whole-document rejection and a surfaced error is a strong control on the only untrusted input the rota accepts; the residual risk is a *valid-but-wrong* rota written by an authorised colleague, which is an organisational matter covered by the named audit trail and the warn-never-block posture. |

### H-060 — An allergy record ended, merged or re-coded in error (allergy cleanup suite)

| Field                           | Value |
| ------------------------------- | ----- |
| **Hazard ID**                   | H-060 |
| **Description**                 | The **Allergy cleanup suite** (v3.212.0, `content-scripts/allergy-cleanup.js`) is the suite's first write surface on the **allergy list** — the single most prescribing-safety-critical structured field in the record. Its four flows (bulk-end of junk/low-relevance codes, duplicate merge, clearing a stale legacy code off a dual-coded entry, and converting a legacy pre-defined-allergy code to a dm+d substance) can, in error: **end a genuine allergy record** (a future prescribing-safety alert never fires; the patient is re-exposed), **merge two genuinely different allergies into one** (loss of one allergen's record), or **record the wrong substance** against a patient (a false alert, and — worse — the true allergen left un-coded). Harm is severe (re-exposure to a true allergen, e.g. anaphylaxis) but always mediated by an explicit clinician confirmation on the record in front of them. |
| **Potential causes**            | A clinician bulk-ends a "too-generic" code that was carrying a real allergy; a duplicate merge combines entries that are related but not duplicates; a wrong conversion target confirmed from a pre-selected suggestion; an async scan resolving after an SPA patient switch offering another patient's entries (cross-patient state); a keeper change clicked while a merge save is in flight; the curated conversion file itself carrying a clinically wrong mapping (e.g. a salt-level narrowing). |
| **Affected users / components** | GPs and clinical staff tidying allergy lists. Components: `content-scripts/allergy-cleanup.js`, `content-scripts/allergy-cleanup-canvas.js` (v3.236.2 — canvas is a new confirmation *surface*, not a new write class), `rules/allergy-junk-codes.json`, `rules/allergy-substance-conversion.json`; endpoints `POST clinical/allergy/end-allergy`, `POST clinical/allergy/change-allergy/{id}`. |
| **Initial severity**            | 4 (Major — loss or corruption of a drug-allergy record can lead to re-exposure and severe single-patient harm) |
| **Initial likelihood**          | 3 (Possible — bulk selection, background regrouping and pre-selected suggestions all create plausible slip paths) |
| **Initial risk**                | 12 |
| **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) **Nothing is ever pre-ticked / pre-staged and no action fires without an explicit user action**; canvas Finalise (v3.236.2) and the retired checklist's bulk buttons additionally show an "Are you sure?" confirmation naming the exact count (Cancel default). (b) **Caution rows never ride a bulk gesture**: they are excluded from "Select all" (retired checklist) and there is no "stage all junk" helper on the canvas — a cautioned row can only be dragged to End one-by-one. Per-instance cautions fire whenever any clinical detail (severity/certainty/reactions/free text) is attached to a too-generic code, and per-code cautions always fire for genuine-but-low-relevance codes ("Allergy to pollen") and for "No known allergies" — **UPDATED 2026-08-23** (explicit user product decision, see the dated addendum below): this caution is now purely informational, explaining that the code is a positive record of a historic check and pointing at the journal as where that check is verified; it no longer argues against, or blocks, ending the last remaining copy. (c) **Merge and conversion are per-entry modal reviews only** — the full current record (severity, certainty, reactions, free text, onset, provenance) is shown before any choice; a conversion requires a live search-result selection plus a separate Convert click. Tile-on-tile on the canvas is a no-op unless both tiles already belong to a detected duplicate group (a merge is never guessed). (d) **Opposite payload-builder invariants, pinned by tests**: the merge builder never changes code identity; the conversion builder never changes clinical fields; the dual-coded clear builder nulls exactly one stale field and **fails closed (throws, no write) unless the edit-form prefill itself confirms the substance is authoritative** (pre-merge review fix). (e) **Patient-epoch guard**: every async fetch/scan captures a per-patient epoch and discards its results if the patient changed mid-flight, so a scan started on patient A can never populate destructive UI on patient B (pre-merge review fix); the canvas additionally pins `_openedPatientId` and hard-closes on a snapshot mismatch (same pattern as the problem canvas); the merge flow snapshots keeper/field choices before its first await so mid-save clicks cannot redirect the write (pre-merge review fix); review state is remapped by group identity when background concept enrichment regroups (pre-merge review fix). (f) **The conversion file is reviewed output** (314 entries, hand-reviewed): suggestions with salt-level ambiguity (depot esters vs oral salts; perindopril's two salt VTMs) are marked not-convertible with explanatory notes rather than pre-selecting a possibly-wrong salt (pre-merge review fix). (g) All writes are credentialed same-origin calls through Medicus's own endpoints under the signed-in user's session — Medicus's validation, ACL and audit fire on every write; failures are surfaced per-row/never silently retried; the page auto-reloads only when every write succeeded so failures stay on screen. (h) **UPDATED 2026-08-23 — the End bin can retire ANY allergy record**, not just junk-classified or "not-an-allergy" conversion rows (this was formerly a hard block; see the dated addendum below for the full reasoning: it is not this tool's place to restrict what a clinician can end in their own clinical system, and the underlying SNOMED history stays in the patient's journal regardless of what the allergy list shows). Every end still requires an explicit drag-to-bin/select gesture and a named Finalise confirmation (control (a)) — the relaxation is about WHICH rows can be staged, not about removing confirmation. The only remaining guard is that a row already confirmed ended this session cannot be re-staged. |
| **Residual severity**           | 4 |
| **Residual likelihood**         | 1 |
| **Residual risk**               | 4 — Acceptable (ALARP) |
| **Acceptability**               | **Proposed — pending CSO sign-off** on the release PR (#253). Deploying-organisation briefing duty: ending, merging and converting allergy entries are clinical decisions; the widget prepares and batches them but the confirming clinician is accountable for each one, and Medicus's own record view (not the widget) is the source of truth to verify afterwards. |

### H-061 — Queue pulse misread as an urgency score or all-clear

| Field                           | Value |
| ------------------------------- | ----- |
| **Hazard ID**                   | H-061 |
| **Description**                 | From v3.236.4 the request/results queue can compress every chip family into one left rail and one named headline (`queuePulseCompress`, default on). A GP may treat the rail as a composite urgency score, or treat a quiet/empty rail as “this row is safe,” skipping the request body. A second red signal hidden behind `· N` may be missed if the why-tray is never opened. |
| **Potential causes**            | Automation bias (H-007 family); scanning by colour only; overflow count unread; fetch-driven chips not yet landed so the headline is incomplete; pref left on without a duty-session of calibration. |
| **Affected users / components** | Clinicians on the Medicus task queue. `content-scripts/triage-lens/queue-pulse.js`, `content-scripts/triage-lens/content.js` (pulse host / why), `hud.css`. |
| **Initial severity**            | 4 |
| **Initial likelihood**          | 3 |
| **Initial risk**                | 12 |
| **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) **No number, no P-rank** — composer picks a named max, never arithmetic (`test-queue-pulse.js`). (b) **Quiet rail is not all-clear** — why-tray footer and aria-label state this; empty ≠ green. Chip-hide (`ch-row-pulse-on`) is **escalate-only** (red/amber); a quiet row keeps its chips so it cannot look cleared. Red is a **solid filled bar** and amber a **hollow bar** (wash fill + 1px edge stroke) in the same rail column — colorblind meaning is fill density/shape, not hue (v3.236.16 crit: replaced the v3.236.4 inline amber ring, which sat on a different visual axis to red and under-signalled amber; both tiers now scan on one axis, pinned in `test-queue-pulse.js`). (c) **Overflow is mandatory** whenever more than one signal exists; why-tray lists every named source. (d) Age / days-open / thread counts / Pharmacy First never own the rail. (e) A mono `RECORD` micro-token inside the headline chip (plus the aria-label suffix and the why-tray line) marks a headline that came from the record, not the request words (v3.236.16 crit: replaced the v3.236.4 filled diamond, whose filled-amber shape collided with the suite's filled=red/hollow=amber severity coding). (f) Pref to restore the full chip pile. (g) Pharmacy First / Ask-back stay on their existing pathway chips (prepare-only; no Done/Sent/Booked). The Act tray was removed in v3.242.2. (h) Absence of a pulse never suppresses the underlying chips (they stay in the DOM; hide is CSS-only). |
| **Residual severity**           | 4 |
| **Residual likelihood**         | 2 |
| **Residual risk**               | 8 — Acceptable (ALARP) pending live-duty review |
| **Acceptability**               | **Proposed — pending CSO review** after a live queue session. |

### H-062 — Wrong appointment cancelled or moved, or a patient messaged, from the organise canvas

| Field                           | Value |
| ------------------------------- | ----- |
| **Hazard ID**                   | H-062 |
| **Description**                 | The **appointment organise canvas** (v3.236.5) is a practice-wide write surface on the live appointment book. A receptionist or clinician can cancel a booking or reschedule it onto another diary. In error this can: **cancel or move the wrong patient** (identity is not "the record open in the tab" — many patients sit on one board); **move an arrived / in-progress appointment**; **also cancel a weekday live booking** if the native cancel form's "other upcoming appointments" ticks were copied through; or **send Medicus's own cancellation / booking SMS or email** if Send-to were left on. Harm is disruption of care (missed appointment, double-book, unexpected patient message) rather than a clinical-record corruption, but it is a write against real bookings. |
| **Potential causes**            | Stale board after someone else moved the slot; drag onto the wrong diary; Finalise of a mixed staged list without reading the confirm bar; copying `otherAppointmentIds` from the cancel prefill (which listed Mouse's weekday Nurse/HCA slot in the capture); defaulting `cancellationConfirmationRecipients` / `bookingConfirmationRecipients` to the form's On options; inventing a same-list or extend write that was never captured. |
| **Affected users / components** | Reception and clinical staff using the appointment book. Components: `shared/appointment-organise-core.js`, `content-scripts/appointment-organise-canvas.js`. Endpoints as CSN W14/W15/W16. Closest prior art: H-043 (commit-time identity), H-051 (reception booking). |
| **Initial severity**            | 4 (Major — a cancelled or misplaced booking can delay care for that patient and displace another) |
| **Initial likelihood**          | 3 (Possible — multi-patient board, drag, and native "cancel others" ticks are plausible slip paths) |
| **Initial risk**                | 12 |
| **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) **Stage then Finalise** — tiles move on the canvas only; nothing is written until an explicit confirm that names each patient, time, source and destination. (b) **Arrived / in-progress tiles are locked** (no drag, no cancel). (c) **`otherAppointmentIds` is always `[]`**. (d) **Recipients default empty; Send-to is a per-action opt-in** (v3.236.15's "Tell the patient" tick, corrected in the log at v3.237.1 — this cell previously claimed "always empty", which stopped being true when the tick shipped): every write sends `[]` unless the user ticks that staged action at Review; a ticked action copies the recipient Medicus's own GET form offers (never invented) and **fails closed** when no channel is offered; the confirm bar names exactly how many patients will be messaged, and says so only when ≥1 is ticked. A **stretch never notifies** — the tick is not offered there because the stretch write sends no recipients. (e) **Stretch** is cancel-then-rebook into a **free** following slot only — "free" now means covered by actual free-slot entries, not merely appointment-free, so breaks/blocked time refuse (v3.237.1); stretch payloads **omit** `allowOverlappingAppointments`; everything the rebook needs is **pre-flighted before the destructive cancel**, and on a post-cancel failure the original booking is **re-created at its original length** — if that also fails the on-screen error states URGENTLY that the named patient currently has no appointment and must be rebooked now (v3.237.1). (f) **Commit-time re-GET**, which since v3.237.1 also proves the **destination** window of a move is covered by free slots on the fresh board before anything is reserved (the captured reschedule payload carries `allowOverlappingAppointments: 'allow'`, so the server will not refuse an overlap — the suite must). (g) **Explicit `patientId`**. (h) **Stop on first failure** — the board is refetched on failure so the canvas shows what Medicus now has, the error names how many earlier actions were written, and the **overlay freezes during the batch** (no second Finalise, no discard/close mid-write — v3.237.1). (i) Paths pinned by `test-appointment-organise-core.js` (241 checks incl. the destination-taken, oversize-drop, post-cancel-restore and release-failure paths). (j) **Sick-day leftover phone list**; similar-slot matching **fails closed** on missing slot identity (an untyped diary is never proposed — v3.237.1). (k) **Book identity pinned at open** — the canvas commits against the site+date captured when the overlay opened and refuses to write if the Medicus SPA has moved to another day or site underneath (v3.237.1). |
| **Residual severity**           | 4 |
| **Residual likelihood**         | 1 |
| **Residual risk**               | 4 — Acceptable (ALARP) |
| **Acceptability**               | **Accepted (ALARP) — CSO signed off 2026-08-23** (Dr D. Triska, in session; hazard-log v3.28). Check the confirm list against the Medicus book before Finalise. The pre-sign-off restriction ("do not use on a live weekday clinic until that review") is lifted by that review. |

### H-063 — "Possibly already saved" hint missed or wrongly asserted (save-attachment-as-document)

| Field                           | Value |
| ------------------------------- | ----- |
| **Hazard ID**                   | H-063 |
| **Description**                 | The **"Save as document" chip** on a triage attachment (`content-scripts/document-file-inline.js`) cross-checks the patient journal for a document already filed for that file (another clinician, another machine, or Medicus's own native upload). A **missed match** lets the clinician file a duplicate document. A **wrong match** (alert fatigue) trains them to ignore the hint, so the one real duplicate also gets filed — or, worse, deters a genuine first save if they treat the hint as a block. The write path itself is unchanged: the chip stays enabled and the clinician still confirms title/type/date before POST. |
| **Potential causes**            | Date window too wide (same-extension document filed any day that week); one journal entry attached to every same-extension chip on the card; `documentDate` being a display string (`"16 Aug 2025"`) or null (native upload) so the first-cut ISO/`new Date()` parse missed or coincidentally matched; `.jpg` vs `.jpeg` alias miss; title-based wording asserting identity the check cannot support. |
| **Affected users / components** | GPs and clinical staff filing triage attachments. Components: `content-scripts/document-file-inline.js`; endpoints `GET /clinical/data/patient-journal/overview/{patientId}`, `GET /clinical/data/document/modals/preview/{entryId}`. No new write behaviour. |
| **Initial severity**            | 2 (Minor — a duplicate document on the record, or a genuine save delayed while the clinician checks; neither is a missed clinical alert or a wrong-patient write) |
| **Initial likelihood**          | 3 (Possible — active patients commonly have same-type documents in any given week; the first cut's ±7-day window made this the common case) |
| **Initial risk**                | 6 |
| **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) **Non-blocking by construction** — the chip stays enabled; a wrong guess can never make a genuine save impossible. (b) **Evidence-stating wording** — "⚠ a .jpeg was filed on 16 Aug — check before saving"; the saved title is tooltip-only, never asserted as identity. (c) **±2-day window** around the task's own created date, not ±7. (d) **One journal `entryId` claimed per attachment** so three photos do not all inherit one saved jpeg. (e) **`parseDocDate`** handles ISO and the live display shape (optional weekday prefix) at local midnight; null `documentDate` falls back to the journal day's title. (f) **`normExt`** aliases jpg/jpe→jpeg and tif→tiff. (g) Preview fetches memoised on `entryId`; a failed preview excludes that candidate only. (h) Hint DOM mutations treated as own (`withObserverPaused` + `_isOwnWidgetMutation` chip-wrap filter) so they cannot start a re-inject loop. Residual limitation named in CHANGELOG: same-day unrelated same-type document can still flag; a dateless journal entry can still miss. Pinned by `test-document-file-inline.js`. |
| **Residual severity**           | 2 |
| **Residual likelihood**         | 2 |
| **Residual risk**               | 4 — Acceptable (ALARP) |
| **Acceptability**               | **Proposed — pending CSO sign-off** on the release PR. Advisory only; no write behaviour is gated on the hint. |

### H-064 — Wrong investigation-report task reassigned, or reassigned to the wrong clinician, from the lab allocation canvas

| Field                           | Value |
| ------------------------------- | ----- |
| **Hazard ID**                   | H-064 |
| **Description**                 | The lab allocation canvas writes Medicus's own `POST /tasks/{slug}/task-list/bulk-reassign` (W23; 404-fallback `/tasks/task-list/bulk-reassign`). A **wrong task** in the batch, or a **wrong clinician UUID** for a chip, moves a result off the shared inbox onto someone who did not order it — the right GP may never see it, and an abnormal result sits unread. The write does not file the result or change clinical content; the harm is delayed or mis-routed review. |
| **Potential causes**            | Name match colliding two people who share surname + first initial; a typed chip with no staff UUID guessed-through; a stale canvas after the queue moved; posting extra/invented keys; treating the lab/org `requester` object or the named GP as who ordered; treating task status as a clinician. |
| **Affected users / components** | GPs and filing staff on the Investigation Results queue. Components: `shared/lab-allocate-core.js`, `content-scripts/lab-allocate-canvas.js`. Endpoint `POST /tasks/{slug}/task-list/bulk-reassign` (404-fallback `/tasks/task-list/bulk-reassign`). |
| **Initial severity**            | 4 (Significant — a high-priority result routed to the wrong inbox can delay action) |
| **Initial likelihood**          | 3 (Possible — bulk name-match against a live queue) |
| **Initial risk**                | 12 |
| **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) **User-initiated confirm** listing every patient → clinician or team pair; Keep planning is the escape; nothing writes on stage or drop. (b) **`canWriteAllocations()`** needs a string `taskList` — the GET envelope token when it is a string, otherwise the queue slug already in the URL; an object token is not posted. (c) **Unique staff or team UUID** from row `assignedId`/`assignedTo` or overview `assigneeOptions.staff` / `.teams`; no match or two UUIDs for the same `personNameKey` (or team name) refuses that chip. Same-person name spellings share one field so a sitting `assignedId` is not stranded on a duplicate. (d) **Exactly the four captured keys** — `assigneeId`, `assigneeType` `"staff"` or `"team"`, `taskList`, `taskIds`. (e) **Re-GET immediately before write** with the page query string; any vanished taskId aborts the whole batch. (f) **Stop on first failure** and name how many earlier groups Medicus accepted. (g) Task-list `requestedBy` wins over the lab/org requester object; named GP is a caption, never auto-placement. (h) Copy never claims Done / Sent / Allocated / Submitted / Booked. (i) **Slug-qualified POST first**; captured literal only on HTTP 404. Pinned by `test-lab-allocate-core.js` and `test-write-path-inventory.js` (W23). (j) **Two write-path defects found and fixed 2026-08-25, recorded retrospectively 2026-08-29:** (1) *silent write no-op* (v3.243.2) — the write button was a disabled no-op whenever "Requested By" was already populated on the task-list, because that state skipped the overview fetch that supplies staff UUIDs; a clinician could press Write and see nothing happen with no explanation. Fixed by harvesting staff from overviews and the today-book `staffOptions` regardless, and by naming a blocked write on screen instead of swallowing it silently — closes a real instance of the silent-failure hazard class (see H-005). (2) *partial-batch board desync* — `commitAllocations` can stop mid-batch after Medicus has already accepted earlier groups; the canvas previously took the generic failure path (showed the reason, did not reload), so rows Medicus had already accepted stayed marked "staged" on the board, and a second "Review then write" could re-send those already-accepted `taskIds`. Fixed: the failure path now reloads the board whenever `result.written > 0`, restoring the failure reason after the reload rather than before it. Both fixes keep the write contract unchanged (same four captured keys, same confirm, same re-GET abort — control (e)/(f)). Pinned by `test-lab-allocate-core.js`. |
| **Residual severity**           | 4 |
| **Residual likelihood**         | 1 |
| **Residual risk**               | 4 — Acceptable (ALARP) |
| **Acceptability**               | **Proposed — pending CSO sign-off** on the release PR. Residual depends on the clinician reading the named confirm list against the Medicus queue before Write. |

### H-065 — Wrong or excess safeguarding/risk note cleared from the patient banner, or a batch fires against the wrong patient

| Field                           | Value |
| ------------------------------- | ----- |
| **Hazard ID**                   | H-065 |
| **Description**                 | The "Clean up alerts" pill + panel writes Medicus's own `POST /clinical/note/change-note` (W24) to clear a note's "Flag on patient banner" checkbox — the same class of write as clinician-confirmed OIR tick-off (W22), but here on **suicide-risk, safeguarding and medico-legal** notes specifically. A wrongly-ticked or over-selected note stops surfacing on the patient banner and in the risks-overview list, so a colleague relying on that banner (without the extension, or on a different machine) no longer sees a genuine risk flag they previously would have. A batch that fires after the clinician has navigated to a different patient (SPA mid-review) would write against the wrong record entirely. |
| **Potential causes**            | Misreading a free-text-only row's truncated preview and un-flagging the wrong entry; ticking "Select all shown" under a filter that matched more than intended; a long batch continuing after the on-screen patient changed; a stale field carried through from `edit-note` that Medicus's `change-note` silently accepts but mis-files (the `flags`/`recordedByOrganisation` reshape issues found during development — see W24); mistaking "flag cleared" for "note deleted" and assuming the underlying risk history is gone. |
| **Affected users / components** | GPs and any clinician viewing a patient's banner in Medicus, with or without the extension. Component: `content-scripts/risk-flag-cleanup.js`. Endpoint `POST /clinical/note/change-note`. |
| **Initial severity**            | 5 (Catastrophic — a genuine self-harm/safeguarding flag silently stops surfacing on the patient banner practice-wide) |
| **Initial likelihood**          | 2 (Unlikely — requires a deliberate multi-step tick-review-confirm flow, but the batch nature and free-text truncation raise the chance of an unintended inclusion versus a strictly one-at-a-time action) |
| **Initial risk**                | 10 |
| **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) **Nothing pre-ticked** — every row is an explicit user selection, including "Select all shown" (still scoped to the current filter, still a deliberate click). (b) **One confirm dialog names every targeted note** (category, description/free-text preview, date) before any request fires — Cancel default. (c) This clears **only** `flagOnPatientBanner`; the note, its SNOMED code, its free text and its risk-category classification (`flags`) are never altered — a wrongly-cleared flag is fully recoverable by re-ticking the same box in Medicus's own edit form, nothing is deleted. (d) **Identity re-verified immediately before every write** in the batch (not only at panel-open) — a patient change mid-batch hard-closes the panel and aborts remaining writes, never fires against the new patient. (e) **Sequential writes, stop on first failure** — a partial batch never silently ploughs on into an unknown state. (f) **Verify-after-write**: each write re-fetches `note/overview` and confirms the flag actually cleared before reporting success. (g) Free-text rows are visually distinguished (italic, quoted, truncated-with-ellipsis) from coded rows so a preview is never mistaken for a full/authoritative description. (h) Full request+response logged to console on any failure — no silent partial success. Pinned by `test-write-path-inventory.js` (W24). |
| **Residual severity**           | 5 |
| **Residual likelihood**         | 1 |
| **Residual risk**               | 5 — Acceptable (ALARP), reflects that the underlying hazard class (a genuine risk flag going unseen) stays Catastrophic in severity even though the confirm-then-verify controls make an accidental occurrence Rare |
| **Acceptability**               | **Proposed — pending CSO sign-off** on the release PR. Given the severity ceiling, recommend CSO specifically reviews the free-text-preview and "select all shown" controls before sign-off. |

### H-066 — Wrong inbound-document or workflow task reassigned, or reassigned to the wrong clinician, from the workflow allocation canvas

| Field                           | Value |
| ------------------------------- | ----- |
| **Hazard ID**                   | H-066 |

A **wrong task** in the batch, or a **wrong clinician UUID** for a chip, moves an inbound letter or team-inbox item onto someone who should not own it — the right GP may never see it, and a document that still needs filing sits unread. The write does not file the document or change clinical content; the harm is delayed or mis-routed review. Treating the registered GP as a confirmed requester, or launching on a results / privacy / EPS queue, would widen the same class of error. |

Endpoint `POST /tasks/{slug}/task-list/bulk-reassign` (404-fallback `/tasks/task-list/bulk-reassign`). |

(c) **Named GP is a grouping caption only** — `homeColumnKey` stays assignment-only; decorate never writes named GP onto `requester`. (d) Confirm copy states the write **does not file the document** or mark it complete. (e) Neither new file POSTs — `createClient` is the lab client. (f) Copy never claims Done / Sent / Filed / Allocated / Submitted / Booked. Pinned by `test-workflow-allocate-core.js` and `test-write-path-inventory.js` (W23 stays on `lab-allocate-core.js`). |

| **Residual likelihood**         | 1 |
| **Residual risk**               | 4 — Acceptable (ALARP) |

### H-067 — Patient-identifiable data shown on a public waiting-room display (Note board)

| Field                           | Value |
| ------------------------------- | ----- |
| **Hazard ID**                   | H-067 |
| **Description**                 | Note is a full-tab display meant for a waiting-room TV or a staff-room monitor. If a public profile painted patient names, initials, appointment reasons or request wording, people in the waiting room would see other patients' identifiable information — a confidentiality and dignity failure, and a likely ICO/CQC incident. A staff-only ops tile (triage inbox, practice pressure, remaining slots) mounted on the same public TV would leak operational detail patients should not see and could be misread as a promise about when they will be seen. |
| **Potential causes**            | Reusing Condor/WR strip rendering that includes names; a "show names" preference added later; a crafted backup flipping the waiting-room profile to staff; the renderer reading raw stream fields instead of the aggregate snapshot; wait times shown as "Mrs Smith · 47 minutes"; the request ticker quoting summaries. |
| **Affected users / components** | Patients in a waiting room (confidentiality). Practice staff configuring the board. Components: `board/board-core.js` (`buildSnapshot`, `widgetsForProfile`, `sanitiseConfig`, `sanitiseYoutubeList`), `board/board.js` (renderer), `shared/io/board-io.js` (import lock), `side-panel/modules/board/board.js` (companion copy). Pinned by `test-board-core.js` and `test-board-io.js`. |
| **Initial severity**            | 4 (Major — identifiable data on a public screen) |
| **Initial likelihood**          | 3 (Possible — the live streams already carry names, and the WR strip shows them in the side panel) |
| **Initial risk**                | 12 |
| **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) **No show-names flag exists.** (b) **`buildSnapshot()` copies counts, wait BANDS, tempo and demand totals only** — it does not copy names, initials, summaries, reasons, appointments or by-staff rows. (c) **Public profiles omit staff-only widgets** even if a backup lists them; shipped profile ids lock audience (waiting-room/message stay public); extra public boards stay public. (d) **The renderer paints snapshot fields and the practice-authored message only** and refuses a snapshot that still carries a forbidden key. (e) **Wait time is a band** ("Most waits are under N minutes"), never "longest wait 47 minutes". The practice sets those minutes, the Busy / Very busy occupancy counts, and the band wording from the Note tab. (f) **Import sanitises** the same locks, including custom profile ids. (g) Companion UI states the public-TV rule. (h) Demo streams plant fixture names so CI fails if they leak. (i) **Public dead feed fails loud** — hide wait/tempo/zeroes; full-face fail-loud screen. Demo mode is excluded. Wording is practice-owned; the fail-loud behaviour cannot be turned off. (j) **Public ticker never announces medical/admin request counts** — demand lines are staff-only even if the Requests-today widget is off. (k) **Staff-board confirm + public chrome lock** — opening a staff board from a public profile confirms; the profile select is hidden on public audience. (l) **Companion flap warning** — "Do not type patient names. This text goes on a public TV." (m) **No show-names or staff-tile unlock** — practice-owned thresholds and tile ticks cannot flip a public profile to names, initials, request wording, or staff-only widgets. (n) **Custom boards and words stay inside the same lock** — extra public boards, renamed shipped boards, and practice-authored copy cannot grow staff tiles or paint names. The optional public-demand tempo toggle is off by default. (o) **The "Requests today" tile (`demand` widget) is staff-only** — corrected v3.251.5; it had been public-eligible since v3.248.0, so control (c)'s "staff-only widgets" claim did not cover this one tile until this fix. Now locked at import, config-load and render, same as every other staff-only widget. (p) **Styles and Standard colours are paint only** — ten structural styles, and ten colour options on Standard. Neither can unlock names or staff-only tiles. (q) **YouTube playlist is practice-authored paint and media only** — off by default; only a sanitised playlist id is stored and embedded via youtube-nocookie. It cannot unlock names or staff-only tiles. Fail-loud still hides the player. |
| **Residual severity**           | 4 |
| **Residual likelihood**         | 1 |
| **Residual risk**               | 4 — Acceptable (ALARP) |
| **Acceptability**               | **Proposed — pending CSO sign-off.** Residual depends on practices mounting the Waiting room or Message profile on public TVs, not Ops. |

| Field                           | Value |

Components: `shared/rx-allocate-core.js`, `content-scripts/rx-allocate-canvas.js`, write owned by `shared/lab-allocate-core.js`. Endpoint `POST /tasks/{slug}/task-list/bulk-reassign` (404-fallback `/tasks/task-list/bulk-reassign`). |
| **Initial severity**            | 4 (Significant — a non-routine Rx request routed to the wrong inbox can delay issuing) |
| **Initial likelihood**          | 3 (Possible — bulk name-match plus even-split against the live appointment book) |
| **Initial risk**                | 12 |
| **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) **Same W23 write controls as H-064** — named patient → destination confirm (staff or team), unique staff/team UUID or refuse, exactly four captured keys. Vanish-check aborts the whole batch if any staged taskId is missing from the merged list. Remaining dest POSTs continue after a dest failure; the failure names how many earlier groups Medicus accepted. (b) **Sibling canvas** — launches on non-routine **and** routine prescription-request slugs (`prescription_request_task_non_routine`, `prescription_request_task_routine`, and hyphen twins). W8 is the overview send-to-routine macro and does not share this page. EPS / cancellation / privacy / officer slugs stay excluded (W21); results stay on the lab canvas; document / `viewContext=workflow` stay on the workflow canvas. (c) **Named GP is a grouping caption only** — `homeColumnKey` stays assignment-only; decorate never writes named GP onto `requester`; Split equally / Top up / Distribute equally ignore named GP. (d) **Split / top-up / distribute are local staging only** — they never POST. Destinations are doctors with a session on the chosen working day (calendar today by default; can be set to tomorrow) **plus any Medicus team the user adds** from `assigneeOptions.teams` (`addTeamColumn`; unique team UUID or refuse). Cancelled sessions skipped; Medicus/rota absences drop out; nurses/pharmacists/HCAs are not destinations when any GP-looking session exists. **Split equally** stages only the unallocated inbox pile. **Top up empty boxes** gives leftover unallocated to dests with the fewest tiles and does **not** move sitting work. **Distribute equally** re-deals in-today sitting plus unallocated so dest totals differ by at most one; away boxes are left unless Share this box. Confirm still lists every patient → destination before Write. (e) Confirm copy states the write **does not issue, sign, or file the prescription**. (f) Neither new file POSTs — `createClient` is the lab client. (g) Copy never claims Done / Sent / Filed / Allocated / Submitted / Booked / Issued / Signed. Pinned by `test-rx-allocate-core.js` and `test-write-path-inventory.js` (W23 stays on `lab-allocate-core.js`). (h) **Write vanish-check uses `fetchRxMergedTaskList`** — inbox GET (page query, `keepMasterAssignee`) plus bare GET of sitting work, same merge as `loadBoard`. Inbox-only re-GET does not contain work already sitting with a GP, so Distribute equally then Write would abort with “the queue changed”. |
| **Residual severity**           | 4 |
| **Residual likelihood**         | 1 |
| **Residual risk**               | 4 — Acceptable (ALARP) |
| **Acceptability**               | **Proposed — pending CSO sign-off** on the release PR. Residual depends on the clinician reading the named confirm list against the Medicus queue before Write. |

### H-069 — Companion outstanding-investigations / open-tasks list misread as more certain than the underlying Medicus data supports

| Field                           | Value |
| -------------------------------- | ----- |
| **Hazard ID**                   | H-069 |
| **Description**                 | The Companion's "Open appts, links, tasks & investigations" section (v3.257.0) surfaces outstanding investigation requests (`isAwaitingResults === true`, from the patient journal) and open tasks (incomplete or snoozed, from Medicus's own per-patient task-list endpoint) on triage-task and, newly, care-record pages. `isAwaitingResults` means "no result has come back yet" — it is not a confirmed signal that the request was ever transmitted to the lab, and no field was found anywhere in the data the extension can read that distinguishes "sent, awaiting a result" from "never sent". A clinician could misread the list either direction: as reassurance the request definitely left the practice, or as grounds to duplicate-request something that was in fact sent and is simply slow. Separately, the open-tasks list excludes the task currently being viewed by matching its real identifier out of the row's `overviewURL` (the row's own `id` field is a different value, confirmed live, and cannot be used for the comparison) — a match failure would leave the current task listed redundantly rather than silently drop a different genuinely-open task. |
| **Potential causes**            | No "sent to lab" field exists anywhere in the investigation-request or journal data Medicus returns, so the ambiguity is inherent, not a bug; a clinician assumes list absence means "resulted normal" rather than "not currently awaiting, or not checked"; `overviewURL`'s trailing path segment format changes, breaking the current-task exclusion match. |
| **Affected users / components** | Clinic-role Companion users on triage-task and care-record pages. `shared/outstanding-investigations.js`, `content-scripts/task-actions-panel.js` (`apiFetchPatientJournal`, `apiFetchOpenTasks`, `taskUuidFromOverviewUrl`). |
| **Initial severity**            | 3 (Moderate — could contribute to a missed or duplicated investigation; not itself a direct clinical action) |
| **Initial likelihood**          | 3 (Possible — the sent-vs-awaiting ambiguity is inherent to the underlying Medicus data, present on every outstanding row) |
| **Initial risk**                | 9 |
| **Controls / mitigations**      | (a) The sent-vs-awaiting caveat is stated in the UI itself, not only in a code comment ("Awaiting a result — not confirmation the request reached the lab"), directly under the heading whenever the group is expanded — pinned by `test-task-actions-due.js`. (b) Both lists are read-only: no write capability, no "resend" or "mark actioned" action offered. (c) Current-task exclusion compares the row's real taskUuid (parsed from `overviewURL`) against the page's own `ctx.taskUuid`, never the row's unrelated `id` field; a parse/match miss is over-inclusive (redundant row) not under-inclusive (a different genuinely-open task is never silently dropped by this logic). (d) The open-tasks fetch requests only `statuses[]=incomplete` and `statuses[]=snoozed` from Medicus itself — completed and discarded tasks are excluded server-side, not by a client-side filter that could be bypassed or forgotten. (e) Both lists inherit the existing H-001-class wrong-patient guard already covering this whole section: the sub-state object is pinned before the fetch and discarded if the page/patient changes mid-fetch. (f) Empty states are named ("No outstanding investigations.", "No open tasks.") rather than blank. Pinned by `test-outstanding-investigations.js` (15 tests, built from 3 real HAR captures) and `test-task-actions-due.js`. |
| **Residual severity**           | 3 |
| **Residual likelihood**         | 1 |
| **Residual risk**               | 3 — Acceptable (ALARP) |
| **Acceptability**               | **Proposed — pending CSO sign-off** on the release PR. Residual depends on the clinician still opening and reviewing the underlying investigation or task in Medicus rather than acting on the Companion list alone, consistent with section 8 of the CSN. |

## 7. Review and reporting

This log is reviewed:

- At every minor or major release of Medicus Suite
- On any reported safety incident, near-miss or anomalous output
- On any annual QOF specification refresh
- On any change to Medicus's APIs that affects data extraction
- On any change to UK regulatory guidance on software as a medical device
- On any change to NICE, BNF, or KDIGO guidance affecting implemented clinical thresholds or monitoring intervals

Reports of suspected hazardous behaviour must be sent to the CSO at **dave@graysbrook.co.uk** with sufficient detail to investigate (date, time, version, module, observed output, expected output). Patient-identifiable data must not be sent by email — use the practice's own information governance channels.

If an incident meeting the threshold of a patient safety incident is identified, it must be managed under the practice's own significant event analysis (SEA) process and reported to the CSO in parallel.

## 7a. Deferred clinical capabilities (built but intentionally not wired)

These are capabilities that exist in the engine but are deliberately NOT applied to any
shipped clinical rule until a stated safety precondition is met. They are recorded here so
the gap is explicit and auditable rather than tacit.

### D-001 — DOAC renal-banded monitoring DEFERRED (2026-06-20)

The `intervalByBand` engine capability now exists, but DOAC must band on **CrCl
(Cockcroft-Gault), NOT eGFR** (MHRA/SPS — eGFR over-estimates clearance and under-monitors
low-weight elderly). Prerequisites before wiring: reliable structured + dated **WEIGHT**
extraction (currently absent) and numeric+unit-validated serum **CREATININE** (currently
free-text). A wrong CrCl that lands in the `>=60` band would **SUPPRESS** needed monitoring
with false authority — more dangerous than no CrCl. Wire only when all Cockcroft-Gault
inputs are trustworthy and freshness-gated.
